title: THE FIRST FRAME
goal: Catch the thought before it becomes the room.
steps:
1. Trigger — A trigger flickers.
2. Pause Story — Do not explain it yet.
3. Capture Thought — Pin the first thought, picture, or prediction exactly as it arrived.
4. Quote — Put quotation marks around it.
5. Close Capture — The catch ends there; no life story, no courtroom, no spiral.
win: ✓ One thought stayed one thought; the courtroom never opened.
supports:
• Exhale after “Close Capture”; loosen the label.
• Pulled back? Touch “Capture Thought”.
• “Quote” — the rule loosened.
• “Trigger” versus “Close Capture”: what eased?
• I can use “Pause Story” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Trigger → Pause Story → Capture Thought → Quote → Close Capture

title: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
goal: A loud conclusion still has to pass inspection.
steps:
1. Imagine Trays — Imagine two trays.
2. Name Sides — Name the left SUPPORTS IT and the right DOESN’T FIT.
3. Sort Facts — Drop only visible facts into them—no feelings disguised as evidence.
4. Switch Sides — Now cover the fuller tray and read the neglected one silently.
5. Balance Verdict — Finish with a verdict that can hold both sides without pretending they weigh the same.
win: ✓ Both trays stayed visible; the verdict stopped being one-sided.
supports:
• Exhale after “Balance Verdict”; let feeling settle.
• Use “Sort Facts” on return.
• “Switch Sides” separates feeling from fact.
• “Imagine Trays” → “Balance Verdict”: what changed?
• I can use “Name Sides” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Imagine Trays → Name Sides → Sort Facts → Switch Sides → Balance Verdict

4. Revise Odds — Pick a new number and remember it.
5. Follow Evidence — Act from the revision, not the original alarm.

title: THE BLAME PIE
goal: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
steps:

title: THE GREY DIAL
goal: Binary thinking hates a numbered dial.
steps:
1. Name Extremes — Name the two extremes your mind is using.
2. Build Scale — Build a 0–10 scale between them and say three real anchor points: 2, 5, and 8.
3. Place Today — Place today’s event where the evidence fits—not where the emotion shouts.
4. Choose Response — Choose a response matched to that exact setting.
win: ✓ The dial found a middle, and the response found its size.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Response”; keep both sides.
• Restart detected: “Place Today”.
• “Place Today” widens the evidence field.
• “Name Extremes” versus “Choose Response”: what eased?
• I can use “Build Scale” before concluding.
formula_flow: Name Extremes → Build Scale → Place Today → Choose Response

title: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
goal: One fact can support more than one world.
steps:
1. Keep Event — Keep the event fixed.
2. Invent — Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Predict Different — Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
4. Earliest — Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Speak Plurals — Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.
win: ✓ Possibilities plural. Prophecy cancelled.
supports:
• Exhale after “Speak Plurals”; leave the forecast.
• On return, repeat “Predict Different”.
• “Earliest” — fear isn’t fate.
• What changed: “Keep Event” → “Speak Plurals”?
• I can use “Invent” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Keep Event → Invent → Predict Different → Earliest → Speak Plurals

title: THE SCHEMA CONTRABAND FILE
goal: Smuggle what does not fit reality past the old filter.
steps:
1. Capture — Catch one event your negative self-story would normally delete.
2. Describe Happened — Say what happened, why it really does not fit the old rule, and which convenient excuse the rule will use to dismiss it.
3. Sign — Sign the entry as usable evidence and reread it tomorrow once—no chanting.
win: ✓ The story became one version instead of the constitution.
supports:
• Exhale after “Sign”; loosen the label.
• Catch restart with “Describe Happened”.
• “Describe Happened” — the rule loosened.
• Difference check: “Capture” → “Sign”.
• I can use “Describe Happened” without becoming the label.

title: THE FORECAST SCOREBOARD
goal: Memory edits its predictions after the result.
steps:
1. Count Hit — Before an uncertain event, remember four items: prediction, confidence %, deadline, and what counts as a hit.
2. Keep Result — Afterward, hold the result without rewriting the original entry.
3. Calculate — Calculate the gap between confidence and reality.
4. Spot the Bias — After five rounds, look for your recurring bias.
win: ✓ Forecast bias exposed. Memory cannot quietly rewrite the scoreboard now.
supports:

• Return once to “Calculate”.
• “Calculate” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• What lost power: “Count Hit” → “Spot the Bias”?
• I can use “Keep Result” without perfecting.

title: MAKE THE ROOM VOTE
goal: Your environment casts ballots before willpower arrives.
steps:

2. Place Object — Place the first object needed for the desired action directly in your path.
3. Add Deliberate — Add one small obstacle to the unwanted route: distance, logout, container, timer, or removal.
4. Let Space Vote — Let the room make the better vote easier.

display.title: MAKE THE ROOM VOTE
display.goal: Your environment casts ballots before willpower arrives.
display.steps:
1. Pick Desired — Pick one desired behaviour and one unwanted default.
2. Place Object — Place the first object needed for the desired action directly in your path.
3. Add Deliberate — Add one small obstacle to the unwanted route: distance, logout, container, timer, or removal.
4. Let Space Vote — Let the room make the better vote easier.

• Re-entry move: “Add Deliberate”.

• I can use “Place Object” without perfecting.

title: LET THE URGE MISS ITS APPOINTMENT
goal: The ritual expects you; do not show up.
steps:
1. Name Cue — Name the cue and the usual calming act it normally summons.
2. Contact — Contact only a manageable dose of the cue.
3. Keep Hands — Keep your hands and attention out of the ritual while the urge changes on its own.
4. Mark Peak — Hold the peak and the first natural drop.
5. Let Learning Land — The learning comes from not doing the old ritual.
win: ✓ The urge stayed loud without taking the wheel.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Learning Land”; let wanting crest.
• Skip replay; use “Keep Hands”.
• “Mark Peak” keeps wanting off controls.
• Compare “Name Cue” with “Let Learning Land”.
• I can use “Contact” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Name Cue → Contact → Keep Hands → Mark Peak → Let Learning Land

title: BODY VETO
goal: Install a movement the habit cannot do beside.
steps:
1. Identify Motor — Spot the first motor cue—reaching, picking, scrolling, biting, clenching.
2. Choose Safe — Use a safe opposite posture and practise it slowly three times.
3. Enter Posture — When the cue appears, enter that posture for ten seconds while naming the urge.
4. Decide Consciously — Then decide consciously.
win: ✓ Habit vetoed. The choice came back online.
supports:
• Exhale after “Decide Consciously”; let wanting crest.
• Restart detected: “Enter Posture”.
• “Enter Posture” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Decide Consciously”: what changed from “Identify Motor”?
• I can use “Choose Safe” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Identify Motor → Choose Safe → Enter Posture → Decide Consciously

title: THE FIRST DRIFT
goal: Relapse announces itself quietly before it becomes a return.
steps:
1. Picture the Path — Trace the unwanted behaviour backward in your mind: first act, private permission, routine change, environment shift, body state.
2. Mark Earliest — Place a red dot on the earliest sign you could realistically notice.
3. Plant Interrupt — Attach one simple interruption to that red dot and rehearse what you will do when it appears.
win: ✓ I found the drift point before the whole slide began.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Plant Interrupt”; no forcing.
• Return once to “Mark Earliest”.
• “Mark Earliest” keeps sensation as data.
• “Picture the Path” → “Plant Interrupt”: what changed?
• I can use “Mark Earliest” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Picture the Path → Mark Earliest → Tell Support

title: ADD THE PREFIX
goal: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.

title: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
goal: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
steps:
1. Ask Danger — Ask what danger the thought is trying to prevent.
2. Thank Intention — Offer a precise thank-you for that intention.
3. Answer M — Then answer: ‘I’m not signing this instruction.’ Choose a matching what matters to you action that keeps any useful caution but rejects the controlling move.
4. Respect — Respect the alarm; decline the contract.
win: ✓ I thanked the alarm for trying to protect me—and declined its contract.
supports:
• Exhale after “Respect”; keep the compass.
• Shortcut: “Answer M”, once.
• “Answer M” keeps meaning in motion.
• Look back: “Ask Danger” → “Respect”.
• I can use “Thank Intention” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Ask Danger → Thank Intention → Answer M → Respect

title: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
goal: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
steps:
1. Picture — Picture two arrows.

title: EDIT THE FONT, NOT YOURSELF
goal: A thought displayed differently can be held differently.
steps:
1. Project — Project the sentence on an inner screen.
2. Shrink — Shrink it to caption size.
3. Move Metres — Move it two metres away.
4. Lower Opacity — Lower opacity, swap the heavy typeface for something ordinary, and place generous blank space around it.
5. Read Version — Read the edited version once, then look at real text nearby.
win: ✓ The thought changed format, and some of its spell broke.
supports:
• Exhale after “Read Version”; loosen the label.
• Skip replay; use “Move Metres”.
• “Lower Opacity” — the rule loosened.
• At “Read Version”, compare “Project”.
• I can use “Shrink” without becoming the label.

title: COMMAND DOWNGRADE
goal: Turn the order into a weather report.
steps:
1. Picture Command — Hear the command exactly as it arrives: ‘Leave now,’ ‘Check again,’ ‘You must reply.’
2. Downgrade It — Remove the command tone and turn it into an observation: ‘An urge to leave is here,’ ‘An urge to check is here,’ or ‘An urge to reply is here.’
3. Reject Authority — Let the urge give you information without giving it authority.
win: ✓ Wanting became a signal instead of an instruction.
supports:
• Exhale after “Reject Authority”; let wanting crest.
• Return once to “Downgrade It”.
• “Downgrade It” keeps wanting off controls.

title: PASSENGER THOUGHT
goal: You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.
steps:

2. Ride Passenger — Invite the thought to ride in the passenger seat—audible, uncomfortable, unedited.
3. Keep Hands — Hold hands on the action wheel and complete the movement while it talks.
4. Who Drove? — At the destination, notice who actually drove.
win: ✓ Thought stayed in the passenger seat. Steering remained mine.
supports:
• Exhale after “Who Drove?”; slow the clock.
• Shortcut: “Keep Hands”, once.
• “Keep Hands” puts facts above speed.
• “Who Drove?”: what changed from “Choose Time”?
• I can use “Ride Passenger” without rushing.

title: RIDE THE CRAVING GRAPH
goal: An urge is a curve pretending to be a command.
steps:
1. Level — Notice its current level and where it moves in the body.
2. Watch Slope — Watch for slope: rising, flattening, cresting, falling.
3. Imagine Urge — Every thirty seconds, imagine the next point without acting on the urge.
4. Name Change — When the line changes direction, name the change.
5. Choose Time — Choose what protects the next hour.
win: ✓ The craving curved; the next hour kept the vote.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Time”; let wanting crest.
• Re-entry move: “Imagine Urge”.
• “Name Change” keeps wanting off controls.
• What lost power: “Level” → “Choose Time”?
• I can use “Watch Slope” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Level → Watch Slope → Imagine Urge → Name Change → Choose Time

title: PAIN PLUS THE FIGHT
goal: Separate the wound from the fist wrapped around it.
steps:
1. Make Two Lanes — Imagine two lanes: WHAT HURTS and WHAT RESISTANCE ADDS.

title: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
goal: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
steps:
1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.
win: ✓ Thirty seconds of closure made the real reaction easier to hear.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Next”; release the score.
• Restart detected: “Reopen Choice”.
• “Reopen Choice” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• Compare “Close Door” with “Choose Next”.
• I can use “Read Protest” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Close Door → Read Protest → Reopen Choice → Choose Next

display.full_ritual:
TITLE
THE SKY DOES NOT BECOME THE WEATHER

GOAL
Content changes; the capacity to notice keeps showing up.

RITUAL
1. Name Thought — Name one thought, one feeling, and one role active now.
2. Say Being — For each, say: ‘This is being noticed.’ Search for the noticing itself—its colour, age, or mood.
3. Rest Openness — If none can be found, rest with that openness for ten seconds.
4. Land in Feet — Return by feeling both feet.

WIN
✓ Weather moved; the sky stayed. Both feet found the room again.

• Exhale after “Land in Feet”; keep the compass.
• Shortcut: “Rest Openness”, once.
• “Rest Openness” keeps meaning in motion.
• Difference check: “Name Thought” → “Land in Feet”.
• I can use “Say Being” while pain stays real.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Thought → Say Being → Rest Openness → Land in Feet

PAUSE
Avoid prolonged self-inquiry if it intensifies feeling unreal or detached from yourself or unreality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RETURN WITHOUT A TRIAL
goal: Drift needs a direction change, not a prosecution.
steps:
1. State Off — State what moved off course in plain language.
2. Delete Adjectives — Remove every adjective about your character.
3. Name Value — Name the value still available, then take the smallest move that serves it now.
4. Check After — Only after moving, decide whether the plan itself needs repair.
5. Skip Verdict — Re-enter the plan without putting yourself on trial.

TITLE
RETURN WITHOUT A TRIAL

GOAL
Drift needs a direction change, not a prosecution.

RITUAL
1. State Off — State what moved off course in plain language.
2. Delete Adjectives — Remove every adjective about your character.
3. Name Value — Name the value still available, then take the smallest move that serves it now.
4. Check After — Only after moving, decide whether the plan itself needs repair.
5. Skip Verdict — Re-enter the plan without putting yourself on trial.

title: CAMERA FIRST, CAPTION SECOND
goal: Experience arrives before the commentary team.
steps:
1. Camera Mode — For fifteen seconds, collect camera data: colour, movement, sound, pressure, position.
2. Describe Event — Then say the event using only that footage.
3. Add Caption — Now add the meaning separately and label it CAPTION.
4. Keep Sources — Keep both; never confuse their sources.
win: ✓ Camera and caption separated. Neither gets to impersonate the other.
supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Sources”; leave the forecast.
• Use “Add Caption” on return.
• “Add Caption” — fear isn’t fate.
• “Camera Mode” to “Keep Sources”: what loosened?
• I can use “Describe Event” while fear stays loud.

display.full_ritual:
TITLE
CAMERA FIRST, CAPTION SECOND

GOAL
Experience arrives before the commentary team.

RITUAL
1. Camera Mode — For fifteen seconds, collect camera data: colour, movement, sound, pressure, position.
2. Describe Event — Then say the event using only that footage.
3. Add Caption — Now add the meaning separately and label it CAPTION.
4. Keep Sources — Keep both; never confuse their sources.

WIN
✓ Camera and caption separated. Neither gets to impersonate the other.

• Exhale after “Keep Sources”; leave the forecast.
• Use “Add Caption” on return.
• “Add Caption” — fear isn’t fate.
• “Camera Mode” to “Keep Sources”: what loosened?
• I can use “Describe Event” while fear stays loud.

FORMULA FLOW
Camera Mode → Describe Event → Add Caption → Keep Sources

PAUSE
Switch to safety action when the facts themselves show immediate risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ENTER THE ACTION
goal: Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.
steps:
1. Choose Ordinary — Choose one ordinary activity.
2. Place Vision — Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. Leave Re — When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself.
4. Stay Activity — Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Enter Fully — Participation, not perfect focus, is the target.
win: ✓ Action got there before perfect focus.
supports:
• Exhale after “Enter Fully”; release the score.
• On return: “Leave Re”.
• “Stay Activity” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• Look back: “Choose Ordinary” → “Enter Fully”.
• I can use “Place Vision” without perfecting.

title: TRANSLATE THE VERDICT
goal: ‘Bad’ is compressed data. Decompress it.
steps:
1. Take Judgement — Take one judgement and mentally translate it into three components: visible facts, personal preference, likely consequence.
2. Prefer Decision — Example: ‘Awful meeting’ becomes ‘Two interruptions; I prefer turn-taking; the decision stayed unclear.’ Respond to the components rather than fighting the label.
win: ✓ I unpacked the verdict into facts I could actually respond to.
supports:
• Exhale after “Prefer Decision”; leave the forecast.
• Pulled back? Touch “Prefer Decision”.
• “Take Judgement” — fear isn’t fate.
• Difference check: “Take Judgement” → “Prefer Decision”.
• I can use “Prefer Decision” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Take Judgement → Prefer Decision

title: THE ATTENTION BOUNCER
goal: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
steps:
1. Spot Arrival — Notice the next thought without following it.
2. Stamp Access — Stamp it REQUESTED, RELEVANT, or UNINVITED.
3. Set Budget — Give only the chosen category a short timer; let the others wait without argument.
4. Return Door — When the timer ends, return to the task or deliberately admit one new thought.
win: ✓ The mental pile-up has a front edge again.
supports:
• One exhale after “Return Door”; redirect attention.
• On return: “Set Budget”.
• “Set Budget” proves one signal leads.
• Difference check: “Spot Arrival” → “Return Door”.
• I can use “Stamp Access” amid noise.
formula_flow: Spot Arrival → Stamp Access → Set Budget → Return Door

title: EMOTION, COMPLETE YOUR ARC
goal: Feelings move differently when they are not put on trial.
steps:
1. Locate Emotion — Locate the emotion in the body and give it a precise name.
2. Permit — Permit its current intensity without feeding the story.
3. Track Sensation — Track where sensation travels, peaks, breaks, or cools.
4. Follow Appears — Follow until one natural shift appears, then choose the action the situation—not the wave—requires.
win: ✓ The wave moved through; the situation was still there to choose from.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Follow Appears”; no forcing.
• Shortcut: “Track Sensation”, once.
• “Track Sensation” keeps sensation as data.
• Look back: “Locate Emotion” → “Follow Appears”.
• I can use “Permit” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Locate Emotion → Permit → Track Sensation → Follow Appears

title: ONE CLEAN WISH
goal: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
steps:
1. Bring Person — Bring the person to mind at a safe distance.
2. Keep It Honest — Choose one honest wish that does not deny harm: ‘May we both be free from causing more suffering,’ or ‘May safety become possible.’ Offer it once.
3. State Boundary — Then state the boundary or action you still need.
4. Keep Discernment — Warmth does not cancel discernment.
win: ✓ Warmth stayed intact without making discernment disappear.
supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Discernment”; release extra load.
• Return once to “State Boundary”.
• “State Boundary” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• “Bring Person” to “Keep Discernment”: what loosened?
• I can use “Keep It Honest” without carrying it all.

title: THE 2% SOFTENING
goal: Your face can send the body a quieter memo.
steps:
1. Release Forehead — Without forcing happiness, release the forehead, loosen the eyes, and lift the mouth corners by only two percent.
2. Keep Expression — Keep the expression believable.

title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
goal: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
steps:
1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and look at one fixed object. Say the order once.
2. Run Order — do A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — do C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, return to neutral and restart instead of speeding up.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the whole code stop.
win: ✓ The body surge lost some of its authority.

title: COOL THE ALARM PANEL

steps:

display.title: THE LONGER OUT-BREATH
display.goal: Make urgency leave through a gentler exit.
display.steps:
1. Breathe Pulling — Breathe in without pulling extra air.
2. Let Outflow — Let the outflow last slightly longer, as though fogging a distant window silently.
3. Repeat Comfortable — Repeat only while comfortable; keep shoulders quiet and jaw loose.
4. Breathe Workable — After several rounds, resume natural breathing and look for one workable decision.

• Catch restart with “Repeat Comfortable”.

title: TENSION’S EXIT PARTNER
goal: Teach one muscle where release lives.
steps:
1. Select Safe — Select a safe body region.
2. Tighten — Tighten it lightly—not maximally—during an easy inhale.
3. Leave Muscle — As air leaves, let the muscle become heavy and wide.
4. Compare After — Compare before and after, then move to a second region only if the first fully released.
5. End Clean — One clean contrast is enough.
win: ✓ I felt one clean contrast and stopped before turning it into a test.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “End Clean”; no breath-holding.
• Skip replay; use “Leave Muscle”.
• “Compare After” — alarm isn’t command.
• What lost power: “Select Safe” → “End Clean”?
• I can use “Tighten” while alarm rises.

title: THE CRISIS MENU
goal: Choose before distress turns choice into fog.
steps:
1. Prepare Five — Prepare five ten-minute diversions across different channels: hands, movement, sound, practical task, safe contact.
2. Select Option — During a spike, select the first available option without browsing for the perfect one.
3. Finish Interval — Finish the interval, reassess safety, then either return or choose support.
win: ✓ Distress no longer has to invent the menu while it is hungry.
supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Interval”; release the score.
• On return: “Select Option”.
• “Select Option” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• Look back: “Prepare Five” → “Finish Interval”.
• I can use “Select Option” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Prepare Five → Select Option → Finish Interval

title: TURN AGAIN
goal: Acceptance is often a direction repeated, not a mood achieved.
steps:
1. Catch Mind — Catch the mind reopening the case against what has already occurred.
2. Name Refusal — Name the refusal without criticism.
3. Rotate Attention — Rotate attention toward the existing fact and the action now possible.
4. Return Wheel — Each return is one turn of the wheel; stop counting after the chosen behaviour begins.
win: ✓ I turned back toward reality once more—and stopped counting when action began.
supports:

• Catch restart with “Rotate Attention”.
• “Rotate Attention” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• What changed: “Catch Mind” → “Return Wheel”?
• I can use “Name Refusal” without ranking my worth.

Acceptance is often a direction repeated, not a mood achieved.

1. Catch Mind — Catch the mind reopening the case against what has already occurred.
2. Name Refusal — Name the refusal without criticism.
3. Rotate Attention — Rotate attention toward the existing fact and the action now possible.
4. Return Wheel — Each return is one turn of the wheel; stop counting after the chosen behaviour begins.

WIN
✓ I turned back toward reality once more—and stopped counting when action began.

• Exhale after “Return Wheel”; drop the scoreboard.
• Catch restart with “Rotate Attention”.
• “Rotate Attention” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• What changed: “Catch Mind” → “Return Wheel”?
• I can use “Name Refusal” without ranking my worth.

FORMULA FLOW
Catch Mind → Name Refusal → Rotate Attention → Return Wheel

PAUSE
If repeated turning becomes compulsive, step away and use ordinary support.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REVERSE THE URGE, COMPLETELY
goal: When the emotion is unjustified, half-opposites do not retrain it.
steps:
1. Check Support — Verify that the facts do not support the action impulse.
2. Speak Gently — Then do its full safe opposite: approach instead of avoid, speak gently instead of attack, straighten instead of collapse, engage instead of hide.
3. Match Posture — Match posture, words, and behaviour until the new signal is coherent.
win: ✓ Desire got a seat, not the steering wheel.
supports:
• Exhale after “Match Posture”; let wanting crest.
• Re-entry move: “Speak Gently”.
• “Speak Gently” keeps wanting off controls.
• What lost power: “Check Support” → “Match Posture”?
• I can use “Speak Gently” without obeying the urge.

title: URGE IS NOT EMOTION
goal: Separate the weather from what it pushes you to do.
steps:
1. Name Emotion — Label the emotion in one word.
2. Hide Name — Name every behaviour it is urging—text, withdraw, shout, spend, hide, check.
3. Safe — Notice each SAFE, COSTLY, or UNCLEAR.
4. Choose Safe — Select a low-risk move that respects the emotion without automatically enacting its favourite instruction.
win: ✓ The feeling stayed as weather; the urge lost its marching orders.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Safe”; let wanting crest.
• Loop back? Use “Safe”.
• “Safe” keeps wanting off controls.
• Difference check: “Name Emotion” → “Choose Safe”.
• I can use “Hide Name” without obeying the urge.

4. Choose Safe — Select a low-risk move that respects the emotion without automatically enacting its favourite instruction.

WIN
✓ The feeling stayed as weather; the urge lost its marching orders.

• Exhale after “Choose Safe”; let wanting crest.
• Loop back? Use “Safe”.
• “Safe” keeps wanting off controls.
• Difference check: “Name Emotion” → “Choose Safe”.
• I can use “Hide Name” without obeying the urge.

Name Emotion → Hide Name → Safe → Choose Safe

PAUSE

title: PUT GOOD ON THE CALENDAR
goal: Positive events need appointments, not vague hope.
steps:
1. Choose Genuinely — Choose one really reinforcing experience; assign it a time, place, and first action.
2. Protect Appointment — Protect the appointment from unnecessary multitasking.
3. Details — While it happens, notice three details worth encoding.
4. Lock It In — Afterward, resist grading whether you enjoyed it ‘enough.’
win: ✓ Good got a place on the calendar without needing a score.
supports:
• Exhale after “Lock It In”; let feeling settle.
• On return: “Details”.
• “Details” separates feeling from fact.
• “Choose Genuinely” versus “Lock It In”: what eased?
• I can use “Protect Appointment” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Choose Genuinely → Protect Appointment → Details → Lock It In

title: FEELING OR FIXING?
goal: Regulate first; solve only what is solvable.
steps:
1. Drop Define — After body alarm drops, define the obstacle without emotional adjectives.
2. Ask Whether — Ask if one specific action could change it.
3. Choose Action — If yes, choose and schedule that action.
4. Return Acceptance — If no, return to acceptance or support.
5. Stop Soothing — Do not keep using soothing when the door requires a key.
win: ✓ Soothing stopped where a real key was needed. The next move became practical.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Stop Soothing”; no breath-holding.
• Skip replay; use “Choose Action”.
• “Return Acceptance” — alarm isn’t command.
• What changed: “Drop Define” → “Stop Soothing”?
• I can use “Ask Whether” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Drop Define → Ask Whether → Choose Action → Return Acceptance → Stop Soothing

title: LET THE EMOTION FINISH ONE CHAPTER
goal: Interrupted feelings keep restarting the book.
steps:
1. Identify Chapter — Spot the current chapter only: sensation, meaning, action urge, or settling.
2. Permit — Permit the next natural chapter while withholding later ones.
3. Pause Meaning — If sensation is active, do not interpret; if meaning is clear, do not act yet.
4. Continue Genuine — Continue until a genuine settling marker—breath change, warmth, tears ending, posture release—appears.
win: ✓ One emotional chapter reached a real ending marker.
supports:
• Exhale after “Continue Genuine”; let wanting crest.
• Restart detected: “Pause Meaning”.
• “Pause Meaning” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Continue Genuine”: what changed from “Identify Chapter”?
• I can use “Permit” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Identify Chapter → Permit → Pause Meaning → Continue Genuine

goal: Safe contact gives fear new data.

title: THE CONTROLLED REPLAY
goal: A feared scene needs a container, not a flood.
steps:

4. Finish Location — Finish by naming present location and date.
win: ✓ Replay closed in the present: current place, current date, current choice.

title: BORROW THE SENSATION
goal: Teach the body that a safe signal is not the worst-case story.
steps:
1. Select Medically — Select a medically safe exercise that creates a mild feared sensation—brief spinning, stair walking, or breathing through a narrow straw only when appropriate.
2. Test Sensation — Predict what will happen, induce the sensation briefly, and observe recovery without usual calming it.
win: ✓ I predicted the sensation, borrowed it briefly, and watched my body recover.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Test Sensation”; no forcing.
• On return: “Test Sensation”.
• “Select Medically” keeps sensation as data.
• “Select Medically” → “Test Sensation”: what changed?
• I can use “Test Sensation” while sensation stays.

title: STAY THROUGH RECOVERY
goal: Stay long enough to learn what happens after the peak.
steps:
1. Highest — During a safe practice round, notice the highest point and the first downward shift.
2. Stay Past Relief — Do not leave at that first relief.
3. Remain Cue — Remain with the cue through a visible recovery phase—steady gaze, slower movement, reduced urge—then end on purpose.
4. Leave After Recovery — Departure follows learning, not panic.
win: ✓ Exit came after recovery—not at panic’s command.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Leave After Recovery”; no breath-holding.
• On return: “Remain Cue”.
• “Remain Cue” — alarm isn’t command.
• “Highest” → “Leave After Recovery”: what changed?
• I can use “Stay Past Relief” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Highest → Stay Past Relief → Remain Cue → Leave After Recovery

title: MOVE THE LESSON
goal: Learning that works in one room may not travel by itself.
steps:
1. Repeat Mastered — Repeat a mastered practice while changing one feature: location, time, cue order, duration, or intensity.
2. Change Again — On the next round, alter a different feature.
3. Map Transfer — Keep a small mental map of where the skill still works.
4. Make Portable — Let variation turn a local success into portable knowledge.
win: ✓ The lesson travelled. It no longer belongs to one room.
supports:
• Exhale after “Make Portable”; keep both sides.
• Use “Map Transfer” on return.
• “Map Transfer” widens the evidence field.
• At “Make Portable”, compare “Repeat Mastered”.
• I can use “Change Again” before concluding.
formula_flow: Repeat Mastered → Round → Keep Small → Turn Local

title: THE TWO-CUE MERGE
goal: Combine mastered signals only after each can stand alone.
steps:
1. Select Triggers — Select two triggers already manageable separately.
2. Predict Joining — Predict what joining them will add.
3. Drop Unnecessary — Contact both at a modest dose while dropping unnecessary escape.
4. Stay Long — Stay long enough to compare the combined result with the prediction, then recover fully.

• On return: “Drop Unnecessary”.

• I can use “Predict Joining” while fear stays loud.

title: FINISH THE LOOK
goal: Defence narrows the world; orientation in the present reopens it.
steps:
1. Let Eyes — Let your eyes move before your head.
2. Scan Left — Slowly scan left, centre, right, behind if safe, and toward an exit.
3. Name Cues — Name present cues of choice, support, and distance from threat.
4. Allow Neck — Allow the neck to follow only within comfort.
5. Place Attention — End by selecting where attention belongs now.

• Before/after: “Let Eyes” → “Place Attention”.
• I can use “Scan Left” while sensation stays.

title: PENDULUM BETWEEN TWO TRUTHS
goal: Regulation can be built by travelling, not staying still.
steps:
1. Find Activated — Find one activated region and another settled or supported area.
2. Move Resource — Touch the difficult region with attention for a few seconds, then move to the resource.
3. Travel — Travel back and forth at a pace that preserves choice.
4. Finish Whichever — Finish on whichever location offers steadier awareness of your location.
win: ✓ Certainty remained unavailable; movement did not.
supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Whichever”; leave it unanswered.
• If it flares, choose “Travel”.
• “Travel” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Find Activated” versus “Finish Whichever”: what eased?
• I can use “Move Resource” without a guarantee.

title: ONE DROP, NOT THE OCEAN
goal: One drop can teach what the ocean would drown.
steps:
1. Choose Tiniest — Choose the tiniest fragment of the difficult material: one edge, colour, word, or body sensation.
2. Return Fully — Contact it briefly, then return fully to a stabilising cue.
3. Find Dose — Hold the dose that allowed recovery.
4. Use Less — Next practice uses the same or less—not an ambitious leap.
win: ✓ I touched one drop of the feeling without turning it into the ocean.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Use Less”; no forcing.
• Pulled back? Touch “Find Dose”.
• “Find Dose” keeps sensation as data.
• What lost power: “Choose Tiniest” → “Use Less”?
• I can use “Return Fully” while sensation stays.

title: TRACK WHAT HOLDS
goal: Support becomes stronger when it receives precise attention.
steps:
1. Locate Bodily — Locate one bodily sign of steadiness—warmth, pressure, uprightness, ease, or a capable impulse.
2. Describe Boundaries — Say its boundaries and changes for twenty seconds.
3. Ask Memory — Ask what memory, person, posture, or environment strengthens it by one degree.
4. Add Ingredient — Add only that ingredient.
win: ✓ One useful ingredient found; the rest can stay off the recipe.
supports:
• Exhale after “Add Ingredient”; let wanting crest.
• Skip replay; use “Ask Memory”.
• “Ask Memory” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Locate Bodily” to “Add Ingredient”: what loosened?
• I can use “Describe Boundaries” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Locate Bodily → Describe Boundaries → Ask Memory → Add Ingredient

title: WAIT FOR THE WHOLE BODY ANSWER
goal: Some experience forms before it can be explained.
steps:
1. Bring Mind — Bring the issue to mind lightly, then pause verbal analysis.
2. Ask Body — Ask the body, ‘What is the whole of this like?’ Wait for an image, phrase, posture, or global texture.
3. Check Whether — Check whether it fits by noticing a small inner yes, no, or shift.
4. Leave It Raw — Leave the answer unpolished.
win: ✓ The body answered before language polished it.
supports:
• Exhale after “Leave It Raw”; leave it unanswered.
• If it flares, choose “Check Whether”.
• “Check Whether” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Leave It Raw”: what changed from “Bring Mind”?
• I can use “Ask Body” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Bring Mind → Ask Body → Check Whether → Leave It Raw
safety:

title: COMPLETE THE DEFENCE IN MINIATURE
goal: An interrupted protective move may still be waiting.
steps:
1. Small — Notice the small impulse to push, turn, step back, shield, or say no.
2. Let Unfold — In a safe space, let it unfold slowly at ten percent strength.
3. Stop Completion — Stop at the natural completion and return to neutral posture.
4. Observe Whether — Observe whether the body receives an ending.
win: ✓ The urge peaked without becoming a contract.
supports:

• Use “Stop Completion” on return.
• “Stop Completion” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Observe Whether”: what changed from “Small”?
• I can use “Let Unfold” without obeying the urge.

title: BORROW THE FLOOR
goal: Let external support do part of the holding.
steps:
1. Choose Contact — Choose one contact point—feet, seat, back, forearms, or hands.
2. Release Extra — Increase pressure slightly, then release extra effort and notice what the surface continues to carry.
3. Name Texture — Name its texture, temperature, and steadiness.
4. Trust Ground — You need not manufacture a sense of ground.
win: ✓ The present regained enough detail to hold me.
supports:
• Exhale after “Trust Ground”; notice the room.
• On return: “Name Texture”.
• “Name Texture” proves the present returned.
• At “Trust Ground”, compare “Choose Contact”.
• I can use “Release Extra” to return here.
formula_flow: Choose Contact → Release Extra → Name Texture → Trust Ground

title: TURN UP THE WHISPER
goal: A tiny movement may be the body’s unfinished instruction.
steps:
1. Smallest — Notice the smallest spontaneous tendency: sway, curl, stretch, turn, reach.
2. Pause Enlarge — Enlarge it by only ten percent and pause.
3. Ask Whether — Check if it brings ease, protection, energy, or nothing.
4. Let Determine — Let the answer determine whether to continue, reverse, or stop.
win: ✓ The whisper became clear enough to guide the next choice.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Let Determine”; no forcing.
• Shortcut: “Ask Whether”, once.
• “Ask Whether” keeps sensation as data.
• “Smallest” → “Let Determine”: what changed?
• I can use “Pause Enlarge” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Smallest → Pause Enlarge → Ask Whether → Let Determine
safety:
PAUSE
Keep amplitude small around pain, injury, or unstable balance.

title: DATE-STAMP THE PRESENT
goal: Give the body proof that time has moved.
steps:
1. Say Age — Say the full date, your current age, location, and who is here.
2. Name Differences — Name three differences between now and the remembered danger: exits, resources, authority, distance, or choice.
3. State Belongs — Touch one present object while stating, ‘This object belongs to the present.’
win: ✓ The mind returned from elsewhere without needing a perfect landing.
supports:

• Shortcut: “Name Differences”, once.
• “Name Differences” moves memory toward then.
• “Say Age” → “State Belongs”: what changed?
• I can use “Name Differences” while staying in now.

goal: Unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.
steps:

2. Place Cannot — Place only what cannot be processed now inside it.

4. Close Container — Close the container and reorient to the next task for today.

GOAL
Unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.

RITUAL
1. Imagine Container — Imagine a container whose lock, size, material, and location feel credible.
2. Place Cannot — Place only what cannot be processed now inside it.
3. Name Stored — Name what is stored and when it will be revisited, ideally with support.
4. Close Container — Close the container and reorient to the next task for today.

WIN
✓ Someone else’s share moved back out of my hands.

• Gently exhale after “Close Container”; orient to now.
• Use “Name Stored” on return.
• “Name Stored” moves memory toward then.
• What lost power: “Imagine Container” → “Close Container”?
• I can use “Place Cannot” while staying in now.

FORMULA FLOW
Imagine Container → Place Cannot → Name Stored → Close Container

PAUSE
Do not use containment to postpone urgent safeguarding or necessary care.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

goal: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
steps:

title: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
goal: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.
steps:
1. Read Bandwidth — Choose your current safe bandwidth: ONE SENTENCE, THREE SENTENCES, or FULL CONVERSATION.
2. Choose Size — Name the purpose that must fit inside that size: acknowledge, request, pause, clarify, or repair.
3. Send Signal — Draft or say only the selected amount. Stop when the sentence limit is reached, even if more remains.
4. Set Reopen — Name when or under what condition the next level can reopen. If you cannot offer one, state that honestly without making a false promise.
win: ✓ I stated that honestly without making a false promise.
supports:
• Exhale after “Set Reopen”; soften the jaw.
• Pulled back? Touch “Send Signal”.
• “Send Signal” keeps clarity above heat.
• What lost power: “Read Bandwidth” → “Set Reopen”?
• I can use “Choose Size” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Read Bandwidth → Choose Size → Send Signal → Set Reopen

supports:

• On return: “Add Small”.
• “Add Small” moves memory toward then.
• Compare “Recall Real” with “Release Gesture”.
• I can use “Find Strongest” while staying in now.

title: MAP YOUR OPERATING WINDOW
goal: Know the edges before you cross them.
steps:
1. Imagine Zones — Picture three operating zones: TOO HIGH, WORKABLE, TOO LOW.
2. Add Earliest — Add your earliest personal signs in body, speech, attention, and behaviour.
3. Picture Fastest — Beside each outer zone, picture the fastest safe route toward the middle.
4. Place Others — Place the imagined path where others can help recognise it.
win: ✓ Past and present are separate rooms again.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Place Others”; orient to now.
• Pulled back? Touch “Picture Fastest”.
• “Picture Fastest” moves memory toward then.
• What changed: “Imagine Zones” → “Place Others”?
• I can use “Add Earliest” while staying in now.

title: STAMP WHERE THE DETAIL CAME FROM
goal: A memory matters without every detail carrying equal certainty.
steps:
1. Pick Detail — Choose one small memory detail; do not replay the event.
2. Tag Source — Stamp it SENSED, INFERRED, LEARNED LATER, or UNSURE.
3. Rate Confidence — Give the detail a confidence word—high, medium, low, or unknown—based on its source rather than its emotional intensity.
4. Keep Core — Picture one core fact that remains reliable and let the other detail keep its honest uncertainty.
win: ✓ The memory kept a reliable core and honest fog around the rest.
supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Core”; leave it unanswered.
• Skip replay; use “Rate Confidence”.
• “Rate Confidence” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• What changed: “Pick Detail” → “Keep Core”?
• I can use “Tag Source” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Pick Detail → Tag Source → Rate Confidence → Keep Core
safety:
PAUSE
Do not force missing details; stop and seek support if the memory becomes overwhelming or disorienting.

title: LET BREATH BREATHE YOU
goal: Remove the manager from respiration.
steps:
1. Follow Breaths — Follow three natural breaths exactly as they occur.
2. Leave Breath Alone — Do not deepen, slow, count, or improve them.
3. Start — Notice where each begins by itself and where it ends without instruction.
4. Let Body — Between breaths, let the body choose again.
5. Witness Motion — Your only action is witnessing what already knows how to move.
win: ✓ The thought moved from identity to object.
supports:
• Exhale after “Witness Motion”; watch the thought.
• Pulled back? Touch “Start”.
• “Let Body” proves thought is observable.
• Before/after: “Follow Breaths” → “Witness Motion”.
• I can use “Leave Breath Alone” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Follow Breaths → Leave Breath Alone → Start → Let Body → Witness Motion

content:
TITLE
LET BREATH BREATHE YOU

GOAL
Remove the manager from respiration.

RITUAL
1. Follow Breaths — Follow three natural breaths exactly as they occur.
2. Leave Breath Alone — Do not deepen, slow, count, or improve them.
3. Start — Notice where each begins by itself and where it ends without instruction.
4. Let Body — Between breaths, let the body choose again.
5. Witness Motion — Your only action is witnessing what already knows how to move.

WIN
✓ The thought moved from identity to object.

• Exhale after “Witness Motion”; watch the thought.
• Pulled back? Touch “Start”.
• “Let Body” proves thought is observable.
• Before/after: “Follow Breaths” → “Witness Motion”.
• I can use “Leave Breath Alone” without obeying thought.

FORMULA FLOW
Follow Breaths → Leave Breath Alone → Start → Let Body → Witness Motion

PAUSE
Use outward sensory contact if breath attention increases panic or air hunger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND THE BUSY HALF
goal: Not every unsettled breath needs a longer exhale.
steps:
1. Observe Ordinary — Observe three ordinary cycles.
2. Rate Inhale — Rate inhale effort and exhale release separately.
3. Phase — Which phase is working too hard?
4. Leave Timing — Ease only that side toward neutral—less pulling in or less pushing out—while leaving timing alone.
5. Check Whether — Check if urgency changes when imbalance decreases.
win: ✓ Comparison lost its right to set my value.
supports:
• Exhale after “Check Whether”; drop the scoreboard.
• Re-entry move: “Phase”.
• “Leave Timing” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Compare “Observe Ordinary” with “Check Whether”.
• I can use “Rate Inhale” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Observe Ordinary → Rate Inhale → Phase → Leave Timing → Check Whether

title: RHYTHM BEFORE DEPTH
goal: Rhythm first. Depth can follow.
steps:
1. Choose Slow — Choose a slow, comfortable pace in which inhale and exhale feel smooth.
2. Use Quiet — Use a quiet timer or gentle movement as metronome, never forcing lung volume.
3. Continue Long — Continue long enough to find a repeatable rhythm, then remove the metronome and keep one easy cycle.
win: ✓ Motion replaced the waiting game.
supports:
• Exhale after “Continue Long”; then keep moving.
• On return, repeat “Use Quiet”.
• “Use Quiet” proves motion is available.
• What lost power: “Choose Slow” → “Continue Long”?
• I can use “Use Quiet” before motivation.
formula_flow: Choose Slow → Use Quiet → Continue Long
safety:
PAUSE
Abandon pacing if it feels restrictive or medically unsuitable.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE EVEN BRIDGE
goal: Symmetry gives attention a simple crossing.
steps:
1. Pick Requires — Pick a count that requires no effort.
2. Count Exhale — Inhale for that count, exhale for the same count, and leave any natural pause untouched.
3. Imagine Pair — Imagine each pair forming equal sides of a bridge.
4. Complete Few — Complete a few balanced crossings, then let counting dissolve.
win: ✓ Noise separated into something the mind can hold.
supports:
• Exhale after “Complete Few”; then keep moving.
• Skip replay; use “Imagine Pair”.
• “Imagine Pair” proves motion is available.
• Difference check: “Pick Requires” → “Complete Few”.
• I can use “Count Exhale” before motivation.

title: ALTERNATE THE AIRWAY
goal: Move attention left and right until state feels organised.
steps:
1. Sit Easy — Sit comfortably.
2. Close Nostril — Without force, close one nostril and breathe through the other; switch sides for the next gentle cycle.
3. Continue Unhurried — Continue alternating with an unhurried hand.
4. Keep Breath — Keep the breath quiet and abandon retention.
5. Open Both Sides — Finish with both sides open and let breathing return to normal.
win: ✓ Left, right, centre: attention finished organised and unforced.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Open Both Sides”; no forcing.
• Use “Continue Unhurried” on return.
• “Keep Breath” keeps sensation as data.
• “Sit Easy” → “Open Both Sides”: what changed?
• I can use “Close Nostril” while sensation stays.

• I can use “Leave Feeling” before motivation.

4. Release Technique — After several waves, release the technique completely.

• Exhale after “Release Technique”; then keep moving.
• Use “Reduce Effort” on return.
• “Reduce Effort” proves motion is available.
• Difference check: “Create Soft” → “Release Technique”.
• I can use “Let Sound” before motivation.

FORMULA FLOW
Create Soft → Let Sound → Reduce Effort → Release Technique

PAUSE
Do not practise through irritation, constriction, breathing illness, or dizziness.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: EXHALE IN CHAPTERS
goal: A large release can become several manageable ones.
steps:
1. Let Air — Instead of one continuous out-breath, let air leave in three soft portions with tiny unforced spaces between.
2. Keep Face — Keep the face loose and never push to empty.
3. Wait Body — After the final segment, wait for the body’s next inhale rather than grabbing it.
win: ✓ The narrative stopped owning every room.
supports:
• Exhale after “Wait Body”; then keep moving.
• If it flares, choose “Keep Face”.
• “Keep Face” proves motion is available.
• Difference check: “Let Air” → “Wait Body”.
• I can use “Keep Face” before motivation.

EXHALE IN CHAPTERS

GOAL
A large release can become several manageable ones.

RITUAL
1. Let Air — Instead of one continuous out-breath, let air leave in three soft portions with tiny unforced spaces between.
2. Keep Face — Keep the face loose and never push to empty.
3. Wait Body — After the final segment, wait for the body’s next inhale rather than grabbing it.

WIN
✓ The narrative stopped owning every room.

• Exhale after “Wait Body”; then keep moving.
• If it flares, choose “Keep Face”.
• “Keep Face” proves motion is available.
• Difference check: “Let Air” → “Wait Body”.
• I can use “Keep Face” before motivation.

FORMULA FLOW
Let Air → Keep Face → Wait Body

PAUSE
Resume normal breathing if segmentation causes urgency or tingling.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BREATHE THE GESTURE
goal: Give respiration a visible partner.
steps:
1. Choose Slow — Take one slow movement with two directions—arms open and close, rise and lower, reach and return.
2. Return Direction — Pair the expansive direction with inhale and the returning direction with exhale.
3. Let Movement — Let movement size follow comfort, then complete one cycle without conscious pairing.
win: ✓ The task lost enough weight to begin.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Movement”; then keep moving.
• Skip replay; use “Return Direction”.
• “Return Direction” proves motion is available.
• Look back: “Choose Slow” → “Let Movement”.
• I can use “Return Direction” before motivation.
formula_flow: Choose Slow → Return Direction → Let Movement

title: THE RETURN REP
goal: Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.
steps:
1. Select Neutral — Select one neutral anchor.
2. Attention — Each time distraction appears, notice where attention went and escort it back without commentary.
3. Count Rather — Count returns rather than uninterrupted seconds.
4. End After — Finish after ten honest comebacks, even if focus never felt perfect.
win: ✓ Ten returns happened. Perfect focus was never required.
supports:
• Exhale after “End After”; release the score.
• Skip replay; use “Count Rather”.
• “Count Rather” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• Look back: “Select Neutral” → “End After”.
• I can use “Attention” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Select Neutral → Attention → Count Rather → End After
safety:
PAUSE
Choose a broader practice if narrow focus increases agitation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE SENSE ROLL CALL
goal: Make the present answer in specifics.
steps:
1. Find Five — Find five distinct colours or shapes, four contact sensations, three separate sounds, two scents, and one taste or mouth sensation.
2. Answer Blue — No generic answers; ‘blue attention’ beats ‘something blue.’ Let the inventory end with the most stable item.
win: ✓ Five senses checked in; one steady detail got the last word.
supports:
• Exhale after “Answer Blue”; notice the room.
• Skip replay; use “Answer Blue”.
• “Find Five” proves the present returned.
• “Find Five” to “Answer Blue”: what loosened?
• I can use “Answer Blue” to return here.

title: EXPAND–GATHER–EXPAND
goal: Move awareness through an hourglass.
steps:
1. Acknowledge — First, acknowledge the full weather of the moment.
2. Breathe Small — Next, gather attention around breathing as a small centre.
3. Widen Whole — Finally, widen to the whole body and surrounding space.
4. Spend — Spend roughly one minute in each shape.
5. Carry Final — Carry the final wide frame into your next movement.
win: ✓ There is space between the mind and what it produced.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Carry Final”; no forcing.
• If it flares, choose “Widen Whole”.
• “Spend” keeps sensation as data.
• What changed: “Acknowledge” → “Carry Final”?
• I can use “Breathe Small” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Acknowledge → Breathe Small → Widen Whole → Spend → Carry Final

content:
TITLE
EXPAND–GATHER–EXPAND

GOAL
Move awareness through an hourglass.

RITUAL
1. Acknowledge — First, acknowledge the full weather of the moment.
2. Breathe Small — Next, gather attention around breathing as a small centre.
3. Widen Whole — Finally, widen to the whole body and surrounding space.
4. Spend — Spend roughly one minute in each shape.
5. Carry Final — Carry the final wide frame into your next movement.

WIN
✓ There is space between the mind and what it produced.

• Gently exhale after “Carry Final”; no forcing.
• If it flares, choose “Widen Whole”.
• “Spend” keeps sensation as data.
• What changed: “Acknowledge” → “Carry Final”?
• I can use “Breathe Small” while sensation stays.

FORMULA FLOW
Acknowledge → Breathe Small → Widen Whole → Spend → Carry Final

PAUSE
Use a non-breath anchor if respiration is activating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RAIN WITHOUT THE UMBRELLA
goal: Meet the experience before trying to change the prediction.
steps:
1. Recognise — Recognise what is here.
2. Allow Moment — Allow this moment of it to exist.
3. Question About — Investigate with one kind question about body or need.
4. Experience — Notice that the experience is present but not the whole of you.
5. Move R — Move through R–A–I–N once; resolution is not a required fifth letter.
win: ✓ The experience was met without making resolution a requirement.

• Skip replay; use “Question About”.
• “Experience” keeps sensation as data.
• Keep one lesson: “Recognise” → “Move R”.
• I can use “Allow Moment” while sensation stays.

title: FOUR PARTS OF ONE STEP
goal: Walking can become a moving attention track.
steps:
1. Place Weight — Slow enough to separate lift, travel, place, and weight transfer.
2. Follow Events — Follow those four events through several steps.
3. Thought — When thought pulls away, rejoin at whichever phase the foot is currently performing.
4. Finish Walking — Finish by walking normally while retaining one point of contact.
win: ✓ Walking stayed ordinary while attention stayed connected.
supports:
• One exhale after “Finish Walking”; redirect attention.
• Skip replay; use “Thought”.
• “Thought” proves one signal leads.
• “Place Weight” to “Finish Walking”: what loosened?
• I can use “Follow Events” amid noise.
formula_flow: Place Weight → Follow Events → Thought → Finish Walking
safety:
PAUSE
Practise only where slowed walking is physically safe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LISTEN PAST THE SOUND
goal: The disappearance is part of the Notice.
steps:
1. Play Safe — Ring, play, or notice a safe sustained sound.
2. Follow Decay — Follow its decay with precision until you cannot locate any remainder.
3. Stay Silence — Stay with the silence that receives it, not with memory of the tone.
4. Let Surroundings — Let the next surroundings sound end the practice.
win: ✓ The sound stopped owning the whole moment.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Surroundings”; leave the forecast.
• If it flares, choose “Stay Silence”.
• “Stay Silence” — fear isn’t fate.
• Look back: “Play Safe” → “Let Surroundings”.
• I can use “Follow Decay” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Play Safe → Follow Decay → Stay Silence → Let Surroundings

title: NOTICE THE NOTICING
goal: Turn attention toward the fact that experience is known.
steps:
1. Choose Sensation — Choose any sensation.
2. Recognise — First recognise its qualities.
3. Ask Verbally — Then ask, without answering verbally, ‘How is this already known?’ Rest with the immediacy of knowing rather than searching for an object called awareness.
4. Return Fact — Return by naming one visible fact.
win: ✓ Awareness noticed itself—then landed back on one visible fact.
supports:
• One exhale after “Return Fact”; redirect attention.
• Shortcut: “Ask Verbally”, once.
• “Ask Verbally” proves one signal leads.
• At “Return Fact”, compare “Choose Sensation”.
• I can use “Recognise” amid noise.
formula_flow: Choose Sensation → Recognise → Ask Verbally → Return Fact

title: THE BREATH HINGE
goal: Rest where one phase becomes another.
steps:

2. Leave Hinge Free — Do not hold or stretch the hinge.

4. Allow Breaths — Visit each threshold lightly, then allow several breaths to pass unwatched.
win: ✓ Starting became smaller than the story around starting.

• Use “Change” on return.
• “Change” proves motion is available.
• What lost power: “Follow Inhale” → “Allow Breaths”?
• I can use “Leave Hinge Free” before motivation.

title: WHERE SOUND BECOMES HEARING
goal: Trace vibration to its inner arrival point.
steps:
1. Listen Sustained — Listen to a sustained, gentle sound.
2. Follow Apparent — Follow it from apparent distance toward the place where it becomes an auditory experience—ear, head, body, or nowhere locatable.
3. Rest Briefly — When the border between outside vibration and inside hearing blurs, rest there briefly.
win: ✓ Sound lost its border for a moment; hearing became the event.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Rest Briefly”; no forcing.
• Shortcut: “Follow Apparent”, once.
• “Follow Apparent” keeps sensation as data.
• “Listen Sustained” to “Rest Briefly”: what loosened?
• I can use “Follow Apparent” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Listen Sustained → Follow Apparent → Rest Briefly
safety:
PAUSE
Choose ordinary grounding if auditory focus feels intrusive or voice-like.

Trace vibration to its inner arrival point.

RITUAL
1. Listen Sustained — Listen to a sustained, gentle sound.
2. Follow Apparent — Follow it from apparent distance toward the place where it becomes an auditory experience—ear, head, body, or nowhere locatable.
3. Rest Briefly — When the border between outside vibration and inside hearing blurs, rest there briefly.

WIN
✓ Sound lost its border for a moment; hearing became the event.

• Gently exhale after “Rest Briefly”; no forcing.
• Shortcut: “Follow Apparent”, once.
• “Follow Apparent” keeps sensation as data.
• “Listen Sustained” to “Rest Briefly”: what loosened?
• I can use “Follow Apparent” while sensation stays.

FORMULA FLOW
Listen Sustained → Follow Apparent → Rest Briefly

PAUSE
Choose ordinary grounding if auditory focus feels intrusive or voice-like.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BORROW THE SKY’S WIDTH
goal: Let vision teach attention another size.
steps:
1. Open Sky — Gaze softly into open sky or another unobstructed safe field.
2. Release Pinpoint — Release pinpoint focus and include the edges of vision.
3. Compare Width — Without forcing calm, compare the width outside with the contraction inside.
4. Keep Wide View — Allow attention to occupy both.
win: ✓ The view widened enough for thought and sky to coexist.
supports:
• One exhale after “Keep Wide View”; redirect attention.
• Shortcut: “Compare Width”, once.
• “Compare Width” proves one signal leads.
• “Open Sky” to “Keep Wide View”: what loosened?
• I can use “Release Pinpoint” amid noise.
formula_flow: Open Sky → Release Pinpoint → Compare Width → Keep Wide View

title: LET DARKNESS BE COMPLETE
goal: Visual absence does not need a replacement image.
steps:
1. Set Darkness — In a safe darkened setting, notice darkness as the actual visual field.
2. Return Unfilled — When the mind manufactures shapes or stories, recognise image production and return to the unfilled field.
3. Stay Briefly — Stay briefly, then reintroduce light on purpose.
win: ✓ Darkness stayed complete for a moment; light returned by choice.
supports:
• One exhale after “Stay Briefly”; redirect attention.
• If it flares, choose “Return Unfilled”.
• “Return Unfilled” proves one signal leads.
• “Set Darkness” → “Stay Briefly”: what changed?
• I can use “Return Unfilled” amid noise.
formula_flow: Set Darkness → Return Unfilled → Stay Briefly
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid this practice if darkness triggers panic, trauma, or perceptual disturbance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE BODY AS INNER SPACE
goal: Trade the sense of a solid block for a more spacious inner map.
steps:
1. Imagine Torso — Imagine the torso and limbs as volumes containing room rather than dense objects.
2. Cavities — Notice cavities, distances, and open intervals inside the body inner picture while maintaining feet, seat, and external orientation in space.
3. Keep Image — Keep the image gentle and anatomically nonliteral.

title: CATCH WANTING BEFORE THE OBJECT
goal: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.
steps:
1. Wait Pull — Wait at the first pull: leaning, brightening, reaching, mental zoom.
2. Observe Wanting — For five seconds, observe wanting as raw movement without completing ‘I want…’.
3. Name Object — Only afterward name the object and decide whether pursuit serves the wider situation.
win: ✓ Wanting and doing are separate again.
supports:
• Exhale after “Name Object”; leave the forecast.
• Use “Observe Wanting” on return.
• “Observe Wanting” — fear isn’t fate.
• “Wait Pull” to “Name Object”: what loosened?
• I can use “Observe Wanting” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Wait Pull → Observe Wanting → Name Object
safety:
PAUSE
Use added support for dangerous cravings or impaired control.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FOLLOW IT TO ZERO
goal: A thought’s disappearance is usually ignored.
steps:
1. Select Naturally — Select one naturally occurring thought.
2. Stay Wording — Stay with its exact wording or image as it alters, fragments, loses relevance, or is replaced.
3. Identify Instant — Spot the first instant when no trace can be found.
4. Let It End — Do not resurrect it to verify the ending.
win: ✓ The thought ended. I did not drag it back for an encore.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let It End”; loosen the label.
• Return once to “Identify Instant”.
• “Identify Instant” — the rule loosened.
• “Select Naturally” → “Let It End”: what changed?
• I can use “Stay Wording” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Select Naturally → Stay Wording → Identify Instant → Let It End

title: NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST
goal: Release both hands of mental grasping.
steps:

2. Relax — Relax the corresponding inner movement without demanding neutrality.
3. Let Content — Let the content remain unowned and unobstructed for a short interval.
4. Act According — Then act according to circumstance, not attraction or aversion.
win: ✓ Rejection became an event, not an identity.
supports:

• Catch restart with “Let Content”.
• “Let Content” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• “Act According”: what changed from “Check The Pull”?
• I can use “Relax” without ranking my worth.

goal: Do not wrestle a harmful tendency on its own ground.
steps:
1. Name Active — Name the active pattern and the wholesome quality opposite with it: cruelty/kindness, panic/steadiness, greed/sufficiency.
2. Act Counter — Produce one thought, posture, and act expressing the counter-quality.
3. Keep Credible — Keep it credible rather than grand.
4. Train — Train the opposite channel through embodiment.
win: ✓ The opposite quality got a real body, not just a good intention.
supports:
• Exhale after “Train”; then keep moving.
• Pulled back? Touch “Keep Credible”.
• “Keep Credible” proves motion is available.
• “Name Active” versus “Train”: what eased?
• I can use “Act Counter” before motivation.

title: STAY AT THE SENSE DOOR
goal: What you notice can occur without being kidnapped by the object.
steps:
1. Choose Sound — Choose one sound or sight.
2. Sensory — Notice the first sensory contact, then keep attention at the doorway of hearing or seeing rather than following associations outward.
3. Return Bare — When the mind travels to the object’s story, return to bare contact.
win: ✓ Story dropped away; bare sensation was enough.
supports:

• Restart detected: “Sensory”.
• “Sensory” proves the present returned.
• Look back: “Choose Sound” → “Return Bare”.
• I can use “Sensory” to return here.

title: ERASE THE OBJECT, KEEP THE CONTACT
goal: Let focus outlive its original target.
steps:
1. Stabilise — Stabilise attention on one simple form.
2. Remove Name — Gradually remove its name, meaning, shape, and boundary in that order.
3. Attend Object — Preserve the ongoing sense of attending as the object loses definition.
4. Rest Briefly — Rest briefly with contact that no longer depends on a clear thing.
win: ✓ The load became a sequence instead of a wall.
supports:
• Exhale after “Rest Briefly”; release extra load.
• Loop back? Use “Attend Object”.
• “Attend Object” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• “Stabilise” to “Rest Briefly”: what loosened?
• I can use “Remove Name” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Stabilise → Remove Name → Attend Object → Rest Briefly

content:
TITLE
ERASE THE OBJECT, KEEP THE CONTACT

GOAL
Let focus outlive its original target.

RITUAL
1. Stabilise — Stabilise attention on one simple form.
2. Remove Name — Gradually remove its name, meaning, shape, and boundary in that order.
3. Attend Object — Preserve the ongoing sense of attending as the object loses definition.
4. Rest Briefly — Rest briefly with contact that no longer depends on a clear thing.

WIN
✓ The load became a sequence instead of a wall.

• Exhale after “Rest Briefly”; release extra load.
• Loop back? Use “Attend Object”.
• “Attend Object” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• “Stabilise” to “Rest Briefly”: what loosened?
• I can use “Remove Name” without carrying it all.

FORMULA FLOW
Stabilise → Remove Name → Attend Object → Rest Briefly

PAUSE
Avoid object dissolution when prone to derealisation or perceptual instability.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS
goal: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.
steps:
1. Choose Precise — Choose an anchor and notice the precise moment contact breaks.
2. Return Instead — Instead of judging the distraction, shorten the delay before returning.
3. Track Interval — Track the interval between noticing and reconnection.
4. Let Practice — Let practice end after one stretch with visibly fewer or shorter gaps.
win: ✓ The practice has fewer leaks than it did a minute ago.
supports:
• One exhale after “Let Practice”; redirect attention.
• Loop back? Use “Track Interval”.
• “Track Interval” proves one signal leads.
• Difference check: “Choose Precise” → “Let Practice”.
• I can use “Return Instead” amid noise.
formula_flow: Choose Precise → Return Instead → Track Interval → Let Practice

title: ENOUGH IS A CURRENT FACT
goal: Sufficiency can coexist with ambition.
steps:
1. Identify Part — Spot one part of the present condition that is really adequate: shelter, breath, effort, support, knowledge, or time for the next step.
2. Receive Adequacy — Receive that adequacy without claiming everything is fine.
3. Choose Non — From this base, choose one non-desperate improvement.
win: ✓ I found one thing that was already enough, then chose from there.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Choose Non”; no forcing.
• On return, repeat “Receive Adequacy”.
• “Receive Adequacy” keeps sensation as data.
• What changed: “Identify Part” → “Choose Non”?
• I can use “Receive Adequacy” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Identify Part → Receive Adequacy → Choose Non
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use contentment to minimise unmet needs or structural harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TRACE THE FIRST SPARK
goal: Find what started the fluctuation before content took over.
steps:
1. Take Recurring — Take one recurring state and move backward through its chain: current thought, preceding sensation, image, memory, external cue, and hidden tendency.
2. Stop Earliest — Stop at the earliest condition you can really spot.
3. Mark the Spark — Notice the point where future interruption could happen.
win: ✓ The spark became visible early enough to interrupt next time.
supports:
• Exhale after “Mark the Spark”; let feeling settle.
• On return: “Stop Earliest”.
• “Stop Earliest” separates feeling from fact.
• “Take Recurring” to “Mark the Spark”: what loosened?
• I can use “Stop Earliest” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Take Recurring → Stop Earliest → Mark the Spark

title: NOT THIS, STILL HERE
goal: Remove identities without attacking experience.
steps:
1. Body — Notice body, sensation, thought, emotion, and role in turn.
2. Keep Perspective — For each say, ‘Observed—therefore not the whole observer.’ Do not claim they are unreal.
3. Rest Unlabelled — After the sequence, rest with what remains unlabelled, then reconnect to name and place.
win: ✓ The present reclaimed one clear channel.
supports:
• Exhale after “Rest Unlabelled”; notice the room.
• Skip replay; use “Keep Perspective”.
• “Keep Perspective” proves the present returned.
• “Rest Unlabelled”: what changed from “Body”?
• I can use “Keep Perspective” to return here.
formula_flow: Body → Keep Perspective → Rest Unlabelled

title: FIND THE FIRST ‘I’
goal: Sense of ‘I’ has an entrance point.
steps:
1. Experience — Notice an experience before describing it.
2. Wait Moment — Wait for the moment ‘I,’ ‘mine,’ or ‘about me’ attaches.
3. Trace Addition — Trace that addition to a body sensation, image, or location.
4. Observe Attachment — Observe the attachment without removing it.
5. Do the Task — The task is detection, not metaphysical victory.
win: ✓ I found the ‘I’ without needing to solve who ‘I’ ultimately am.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Do the Task”; no forcing.
• Return once to “Trace Addition”.
• “Observe Attachment” keeps sensation as data.
• Compare “Experience” with “Do the Task”.
• I can use “Wait Moment” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Experience → Wait Moment → Trace Addition → Observe Attachment → Do the Task

title: THE FIVE-LAYER INSPECTION
goal: Identity may be wearing several visible coats.
steps:
1. Move Body — Move through body, energy, mind, intellect, and deep ease.
2. Ask Change — At each layer ask what is present, what changes, and how it is known.
3. Keep All Layers — Do not discard any layer.
4. Place Like — Place them like translucent sheets within awareness, then select the layer needed for practical action.
win: ✓ Five layers became one usable next layer.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Place Like”; no forcing.
• Restart detected: “Keep All Layers”.
• “Keep All Layers” keeps sensation as data.
• What lost power: “Move Body” → “Place Like”?
• I can use “Ask Change” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Move Body → Ask Change → Keep All Layers → Place Like
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid abstract layer work when immediate grounding is needed.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE
goal: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
steps:
1. Pick Word — Choose one harmless five-letter word, such as TABLE. Use each letter once; there is no need to finish perfectly.
2. Call Object — For the first letter, name a neutral object beginning with it—T for tree, for example.
3. Flash Image — Picture that object for about two seconds with no action, meaning, memory, or story.
4. Jump Letter — Jump to the next letter and a completely unrelated object. End after five letters; do not score sleep.
win: ✓ I ended after five letters; do not score sleep.
supports:
• Exhale after “Jump Letter”; loosen the label.
• Skip replay; use “Flash Image”.
• “Flash Image” — the rule loosened.
• What lost power: “Pick Word” → “Jump Letter”?
• I can use “Call Object” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Pick Word → Call Object → Flash Image → Jump Letter
safety:
PAUSE
Use only while safely resting; never while driving. Stop if images become distressing, compulsive, or disorienting.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REMOVE THE NAME BADGES
goal: See what remains when roles clock out briefly.
steps:
1. Name — Name the roles active today. Keep the pace deliberately slow here.
2. Imagine Badge — One by one, imagine placing each badge on a table—parent, worker, partner, achiever, patient, helper.
3. Release Roles — Sit without using any badge to answer ‘Who am I now?’ After a short pause, reclaim only the role needed next.
win: ✓ I took the name badges off and noticed I was still here.
supports:
• Exhale after “Release Roles”; leave the forecast.
• Pulled back? Touch “Imagine Badge”.
• “Imagine Badge” — fear isn’t fate.
• Keep one lesson: “Name” → “Release Roles”.
• I can use “Imagine Badge” while fear stays loud.

title: CLEAN ACTION, OPEN HANDS
goal: Own the quality of the move, not the universe’s reply.
steps:
1. Look Like — Define what right action looks like in process terms: honest words, careful preparation, timely follow-through.
2. Place Outside — Specify the outcome you hope for, then place it outside the scoring system.
3. Judge the Action — Judge today only by whether the action met its standard.
win: ✓ I did the clean action and left the outcome with open hands.
supports:

• Shortcut: “Place Outside”, once.
• “Place Outside” puts facts above speed.
• Look back: “Look Like” → “Judge the Action”.
• I can use “Place Outside” without rushing.

CLEAN ACTION, OPEN HANDS

GOAL
Own the quality of the move, not the universe’s reply.

RITUAL
1. Look Like — Define what right action looks like in process terms: honest words, careful preparation, timely follow-through.
2. Place Outside — Specify the outcome you hope for, then place it outside the scoring system.
3. Judge the Action — Judge today only by whether the action met its standard.

WIN
✓ I did the clean action and left the outcome with open hands.

• Exhale after “Judge the Action”; slow the clock.
• Shortcut: “Place Outside”, once.
• “Place Outside” puts facts above speed.
• Look back: “Look Like” → “Judge the Action”.
• I can use “Place Outside” without rushing.

FORMULA FLOW
Look Like → Place Outside → Judge the Action

PAUSE
Results still matter when they reveal harm, error, or a need to change course.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHAT REMAINS WHEN REWARD LEAVES?
goal: Duty becomes clearer after fear and praise exit the room.
steps:
1. Name Role — Name your role, the people affected, and the values governing it.
2. Remove Applause — Mentally remove applause, punishment, and personal advantage.
3. Ask Responsibility — Ask which responsibility still stands.
4. Set Role Limit — Convert that answer into a time-bound action and one limit on what the role does not require.
win: ✓ The reward disappeared; the part I still cared about stayed.
supports:
• Exhale after “Set Role Limit”; keep the compass.
• If it flares, choose “Ask Responsibility”.
• “Ask Responsibility” keeps meaning in motion.
• At “Set Role Limit”, compare “Name Role”.
• I can use “Remove Applause” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Name Role → Remove Applause → Ask Responsibility → Set Role Limit

title: SAME VALUE, TWO OUTCOMES
goal: Stability is trained before the verdict arrives.
steps:
1. Imagine Action — Imagine the action succeeding.
2. State Governing — State what that value asks of you next.
3. Imagine Failing — Imagine it failing.
4. State Value — State how the same value responds there.
5. Let Outcome — Let outcome alter strategy, not your ethical centre.
win: ✓ Meaning found a next move without denying the pain.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Outcome”; keep both sides.
• Pulled back? Touch “Imagine Failing”.
• “State Value” widens the evidence field.
• Keep one lesson: “Imagine Action” → “Let Outcome”.
• I can use “State Governing” before concluding.
formula_flow: Imagine Action → State Governing → Imagine Failing → State Value → Let Outcome

title: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
goal: A throwaway mistake can make the first move lose its authority.
steps:
1. Throwaway — Open a private mental sandbox and mark it THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING.
2. Make Wrong — Imagine one obviously imperfect start: a clumsy first sentence, rough title, messy mental sketch, or unfinished opening.
3. Fix One — Correct exactly one useful part without polishing the rest.
4. Continue Clean — Keep working only if the task now feels editable; otherwise keep the corrected fragment in mind and stop cleanly.
win: ✓ The work can move without earning a flawless score first.
supports:
• Exhale after “Continue Clean”; release the score.
• Skip replay; use “Fix One”.
• “Fix One” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Continue Clean”: what changed from “Throwaway”?
• I can use “Make Wrong” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Throwaway → Make Wrong → Fix One → Continue Clean

A throwaway mistake can make the first move lose its authority.

RITUAL
1. Throwaway — Open a private mental sandbox and mark it THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING.
2. Make Wrong — Imagine one obviously imperfect start: a clumsy first sentence, rough title, messy mental sketch, or unfinished opening.
3. Fix One — Correct exactly one useful part without polishing the rest.
4. Continue Clean — Keep working only if the task now feels editable; otherwise keep the corrected fragment in mind and stop cleanly.

WIN
✓ The work can move without earning a flawless score first.

• Exhale after “Continue Clean”; release the score.
• Skip replay; use “Fix One”.
• “Fix One” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Continue Clean”: what changed from “Throwaway”?
• I can use “Make Wrong” without perfecting.

FORMULA FLOW
Throwaway → Make Wrong → Fix One → Continue Clean

PAUSE
Never use deliberate errors in medical, legal, financial, safety-critical, submitted, or live shared work.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ALLY OR SABOTEUR?
goal: Judge the mental move by how it treats your life.
steps:
1. Ask Thought — Ask the current thought three questions: Does it clarify the next move?
2. Check Protection — Does it protect something real?
3. Leave Me — Does it leave me more capable afterward?
4. Score Yes — Score each yes or no.
5. Thank Warning — If it fails two, thank the warning and appoint a different inner adviser.
win: ✓ Kept the warning, fired the sabotage, and chose a better adviser.
supports:
• Exhale after “Thank Warning”; slow the clock.
• Return once to “Leave Me”.
• “Score Yes” puts facts above speed.
• What lost power: “Ask Thought” → “Thank Warning”?
• I can use “Check Protection” without rushing.
