display.full_ritual:
TITLE
THE SUSTAINABLE MIDDLE

GOAL
Extremes can impersonate discipline.

RITUAL
1. Rest Review — Review sleep, food, effort, practice, and rest.
2. Find Area — Find the area swinging between too much and too little.
3. Set Middle — Set a middle range you could repeat for two weeks.
4. Choose Smallest — Use the smallest adjustment that moves into that band today.

WIN
✓ The ignored side regained a vote.

• Exhale after “Choose Smallest”; keep both sides.
• Return once to “Set Middle”.
• “Set Middle” widens the evidence field.
• Look back: “Rest Review” → “Choose Smallest”.
• I can use “Find Area” before concluding.

FORMULA FLOW
Rest Review → Find Area → Set Middle → Choose Smallest

PAUSE
Medical and nutritional needs should override generic moderation advice.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DEDICATE THE MOVE
goal: A larger recipient can change the flavour of effort.
steps:
1. Select Behaviour — Select a behaviour; spot who or what it serves beyond immediate reward: a child, patient, craft, community, future generation, or principle.
2. Act Offering — do the act as an offering to that recipient.
3. Keep Quality — Keep quality high even if nobody knows.
win: ✓ The effort felt different once it belonged to something larger than me.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Keep Quality”; no forcing.
• Return once to “Act Offering”.
• “Act Offering” keeps sensation as data.
• “Keep Quality”: what changed from “Select Behaviour”?
• I can use “Act Offering” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Select Behaviour → Act Offering → Keep Quality

title: THE WAKING DREAM CHECK
goal: Meaning builds worlds more quickly than we notice.
steps:
1. Take Event — Take one rigid reading of an event.
2. Compare Dream — Compare it with a dream: both organise fragments into a convincing world.
3. Identify Facts — Spot which facts are raw and which connections were constructed.
4. Try Construction — Try one alternate construction and observe how lived experience changes.
win: ✓ Another person’s response moved out of the judge’s chair.
supports:
• Exhale after “Try Construction”; drop the scoreboard.
• Return once to “Identify Facts”.
• “Identify Facts” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• At “Try Construction”, compare “Take Event”.
• I can use “Compare Dream” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Take Event → Compare Dream → Identify Facts → Try Construction
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid dreamlike framing if it increases derealisation or psychotic symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND WHERE THE PATTERN MISSED
goal: One exception is enough to weaken inevitability.
steps:
1. Name Pattern — Name the recurring pattern in one line, including the trigger and usual response.
2. Find Misses — Find two occasions when the same kind of trigger produced no pattern or a clearly weaker version.
3. Compare Conditions — Compare the exceptions. Spot one shared condition that you can influence: timing, preparation, company, distance, information, or body care.
4. Transplant Edge — Place that condition into the next comparable situation and define what weaker would look like.
win: ✓ The pattern already has an exception; inevitability just lost ground.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Transplant Edge”; no forcing.
• Loop back? Use “Compare Conditions”.
• “Compare Conditions” keeps sensation as data.
• At “Transplant Edge”, compare “Name Pattern”.
• I can use “Find Misses” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Name Pattern → Find Misses → Compare Conditions → Transplant Edge
safety:
PAUSE
Exceptions do not make unsafe situations safe; do not use this game to blame yourself for trauma, illness, abuse, discrimination, or coercion.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: STOP RENEWING THE CONSTRUCTION
goal: Some mental worlds persist through continuous subscription.
steps:

2. Time — For one minute, refuse only the renewal: no new scene, argument, or confirmation.
3. Let Existing — Let existing residue fade at its own rate.
4. Redirect — Redirect the freed attention into a chosen sensory task.
win: ✓ The construction crew clocked off; attention returned to the real room.
supports:

• Loop back? Use “Let Existing”.
• “Let Existing” proves the present returned.
• “Identify Image” to “Redirect”: what loosened?
• I can use “Time” to return here.

title: RETURN THE PROJECTION TO SENDER
goal: The mind may be viewing its expectation on someone else’s screen.
steps:
1. Picture Quality — Picture the quality you are assigning outward.
2. Ask Internal — Ask what internal expectation, fear, or rule would make that quality especially visible.
3. Name External — Name the external evidence separately.
4. Keep Facts — Keep what the facts support; return the excess meaning to your own inquiry.
win: ✓ Facts stayed; the extra projection went back for review.
supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Facts”; soften the jaw.
• Re-entry move: “Name External”.

title: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
goal: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.
steps:
1. Wait Thought — Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. Empty — At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest Duration — Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Let Thought — Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count Gap — Count the gap only after it is over.
win: ✓ What matters stayed reachable inside the loss.
supports:
• Exhale after “Count Gap”; keep the compass.
• Pulled back? Touch “Rest Duration”.
• “Let Thought” keeps meaning in motion.
• What changed: “Wait Thought” → “Count Gap”?
• I can use “Empty” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Wait Thought → Empty → Rest Duration → Let Thought → Count Gap

title: RUN THE START GATE TWICE
goal: The first start can be rehearsal; the second one becomes real.
steps:
1. Stage Door — Choose the opening movements: open the file, place the tool, find the line, or position your hands. Keep it under ten seconds.

3. Full Reset — Return your hands or screen to neutral exactly once. Leave the plan unchanged or add another rehearsal.
4. Live Entry — Repeat the same sequence and continue straight into thirty seconds of real work.

title: DIFFERENCE INSIDE ONE FIELD
goal: Diversity need not become division.
steps:
1. Contrasting — Notice two contrasting experiences—pleasant and painful, self and other, sound and silence.
2. Hold Distinct — Hold their distinct qualities without merging them.
3. Include Shared — Then include the shared field in which both are present.
4. Let Difference — Let difference remain vivid without translating it into separation.
win: ✓ Difference stayed visible; separation never became necessary.

title: PRECISE OUTSIDE, QUIET INSIDE
goal: Action can be sharp without inner warfare.
steps:
1. Define — Set the exact external behaviour required.
2. Execute — Execute it with full timing and skill.
3. Imagine Applause — Meanwhile, decline the running argument about authorship, resentment, or imagined applause.
4. Let Body — Allow the body act and the inner courtroom remain closed until the task ends.
win: ✓ The action stayed precise while the inner courtroom stayed closed.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Let Body”; no forcing.
• Shortcut: “Imagine Applause”, once.
• “Imagine Applause” keeps sensation as data.
• Difference check: “Define” → “Let Body”.
• I can use “Execute” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Define → Execute → Imagine Applause → Let Body

title: BOX THE PROBLEM
goal: Scattered distress cannot be solved because it has no edges.
steps:
1. Picture Lines — Picture three lines: CURRENT CONDITION; DESIRED CONDITION; MEASURABLE GAP.
2. Remove History — Remove history unless it changes the gap.
3. Give Problem — Give the problem a time horizon and one owner.
4. Statement — If the statement still contains ‘everything,’ shrink it again.
win: ✓ I boxed the problem until ‘everything’ could no longer fit inside it.
supports:
• Exhale after “Statement”; soften the jaw.
• Re-entry move: “Give Problem”.
• “Give Problem” keeps clarity above heat.
• Difference check: “Picture Lines” → “Statement”.
• I can use “Remove History” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Picture Lines → Remove History → Give Problem → Statement

title: FIXED, FLEXIBLE, UNKNOWN, ASSUMED
goal: Obstacles demand different tools depending on their category.
steps:
1. Name — Name every barrier.
2. Mark Category — Mark each barrier as fixed, flexible, unknown, or assumed.
3. Test Assumed — Accept the fixed, negotiate the flexible, investigate the unknown, and test the assumed.
4. Start What Moves — Begin with the highest-impact item whose category permits movement.
win: ✓ Care stayed; over-ownership did not.
supports:
• Exhale after “Start What Moves”; release extra load.
• On return: “Test Assumed”.
• “Test Assumed” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• “Name” to “Start What Moves”: what loosened?
• I can use “Mark Category” without carrying it all.

title: THE NO-JUDGEMENT OPTION STORM
goal: Evaluation kills possibilities before they are born.
steps:
1. Start Brief — Start a brief timer and generate options without ranking, explaining, or defending them.
2. Include Conventional — Include one conventional, one tiny, one reversible, one collaborative, and one strange-but-safe possibility.
3. Test Feasibility — Only after the timer ends may feasibility enter the room.
win: ✓ I let options multiply before judgement was allowed into the room.
supports:
• Exhale after “Test Feasibility”; soften the jaw.
• On return: “Include Conventional”.
• “Include Conventional” keeps clarity above heat.
• What changed: “Start Brief” → “Test Feasibility”?
• I can use “Include Conventional” without extra heat.

title: DECIDE THE STOPPING LINE FIRST
goal: Analysis cannot finish if ‘enough’ has no definition.
steps:
1. State Minimum — Before researching, state the minimum evidence required to choose: number of quotes, critical facts, confidence level, or deadline.
2. Picture Genuinely — Picture what would really reverse the decision.
3. Select Further — When the threshold is met, select; further information needs a new reason for entry.

supports:

• On return: “Picture Genuinely”.
• “Picture Genuinely” keeps clarity above heat.
• At “Select Further”, compare “State Minimum”.
• I can use “Picture Genuinely” without extra heat.

title: IMPACT IS KNOWN; MOTIVE IS PENDING
goal: Do not let mind-reading erase visible harm.
steps:

title: THE FOUR-PART LIMIT
goal: A boundary becomes real when follow-through is inside your control.
steps:
1. State Triggering — State the triggering condition, your limit, the action you will take, and when you will take it.
2. Remove Threats — Remove threats that depend on the other person changing.
3. Practise Line — Practise the line once at speaking volume, then prepare the consequence before delivery.
win: ✓ My boundary now includes the part I can actually enforce.
supports:
• Exhale after “Practise Line”; release extra load.
• Re-entry move: “Remove Threats”.
• “Remove Threats” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• “State Triggering” → “Practise Line”: what changed?
• I can use “Remove Threats” without carrying it all.

title: ROTATE THE CHAIR
goal: One perspective is data, not the whole room.
steps:
1. Describe Event — Describe the event from your position.
2. Move Seats — Move seats and say what the other person might perceive, labelling guesses.
3. Watch Behaviour — Stand as a neutral observer and keep only observable behaviour.
4. Ask Future — Finally, ask what future-you would wish had happened next.
win: ✓ The conversation gained structure instead of more force.
supports:
• Exhale after “Ask Future”; soften the jaw.
• On return: “Watch Behaviour”.
• “Watch Behaviour” keeps clarity above heat.
• “Ask Future”: what changed from “Describe Event”?

title: MOTIVE: ACCESS DENIED
goal: Other minds are opaque until they speak and behave.
steps:
1. Catch Sentence — Catch the sentence ‘They think…’ or ‘They wanted…’.
2. Replace Possibilities — Replace it with three possibilities and one clear question.
3. Possibility — Notice each possibility as hypothesis, not evidence.
4. Choose Behaviour — Choose behaviour based on what is known while curiosity remains active.
win: ✓ Curiosity stayed open without pretending I could read another mind.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Behaviour”; soften the jaw.
• Catch restart with “Possibility”.
• “Possibility” keeps clarity above heat.
• What lost power: “Catch Sentence” → “Choose Behaviour”?
• I can use “Replace Possibilities” without extra heat.

title: CARE WITHOUT CARRYING
goal: Empathy can cross a boundary; obligation must show its passport.
steps:
1. Separate Feelings — Name the other person’s feeling and your own current feeling separately.
2. Locate Relative — Locate each relative to your body.
3. Ask Compassionate — Ask what compassionate action is actually yours and what emotional work remains theirs.
4. Care Without Carrying — Offer the first without absorbing the second.
win: ✓ The boundary became visible without turning cold.
supports:
• Exhale after “Care Without Carrying”; release extra load.
• Pulled back? Touch “Ask Compassionate”.
• “Ask Compassionate” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Look back: “Separate Feelings” → “Care Without Carrying”.
• I can use “Locate Relative” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Separate Feelings → Locate Relative → Ask Compassionate → Care Without Carrying

title: THE FIVE-BRICK REPAIR
goal: Reconnection is built from specific materials.
steps:
1. Build Repair — Build five bricks in order: the event without spin; the impact without defence; your responsibility without dilution; the unmet need; one concrete repair action.
2. Ask Evidence — Decide what changed behaviour would look like over time.
3. Make It Real — Treat the apology as the doorway and the changed behaviour as the proof.
win: ✓ I rebuilt repair from five bricks, not from one polished apology.
supports:

• Re-entry move: “Ask Evidence”.
• “Ask Evidence” keeps blame in proportion.
• “Make It Real”: what changed from “Build Repair”?
• I can use “Ask Evidence” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Build Repair → Ask Evidence → Apology

title: SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT.
goal: Give the feeling space without sending it to the other person.
steps:
1. See The Person — Imagine the person in front of you.
2. Say What Happened — In your mind, say what happened, what you felt, what you needed, and what you now choose to release.
3. Do Not Edit — Let the message be honest, but do not plan harm.
4. Wait — Do not contact the person for twenty-four hours. Let the message stay only in your mind.
win: ✓ I let the message stay only in my mind.
supports:
• Exhale after “Wait”; soften the jaw.
• Re-entry move: “Do Not Edit”.
• “Do Not Edit” keeps clarity above heat.
• At “Wait”, compare “See The Person”.
• I can use “Say What Happened” without extra heat.

TITLE

GOAL
Give the feeling space without sending it to the other person.

RITUAL
1. See The Person — Imagine the person in front of you.

3. Do Not Edit — Let the message be honest, but do not plan harm.
4. Wait — Do not contact the person for twenty-four hours. Let the message stay only in your mind.

WIN
✓ I let the message stay only in my mind.

• Exhale after “Wait”; soften the jaw.
• Re-entry move: “Do Not Edit”.
• “Do Not Edit” keeps clarity above heat.
• At “Wait”, compare “See The Person”.
• I can use “Say What Happened” without extra heat.

FORMULA FLOW
See The Person → Say What Happened → Do Not Edit → Wait

PAUSE
Stop and seek support if the exercise increases revenge thoughts, fear, or trauma.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE TWENTY-MINUTE TRUTH STORY
goal: A private story can help your mind make sense of an event.
steps:
1. Set A Time — Choose up to twenty minutes.
2. Tell The Story — In your mind, move through what occurred, what you felt, and what it means now.
3. Return to Now — End by naming your location, today’s date, and one caring action you can take.
4. Repeat if Useful — Try again on another day only if it helps.
win: ✓ The story got a container, an ending, and permission to stay private.
supports:
• Exhale after “Repeat if Useful”; loosen the label.
• Use “Return to Now” on return.
• “Return to Now” — the rule loosened.
• Before/after: “Set A Time” → “Repeat if Useful”.
• I can use “Tell The Story” without becoming the label.

title: TWO CHAIRS, NO TELEPATHY
goal: Give both positions a voice without claiming either is fact.
steps:
1. Place Chairs — Place two chairs apart.
2. Speak Position — Speak from your position using first person.
3. Switch Chair — Move and answer as the other position, labelling imagination where knowledge is missing.
4. Return To Facts — Return to your chair and state what changed, what did not, and what real conversation may still be needed.
win: ✓ The next sentence can carry the boundary without carrying the fight.
supports:
• Exhale after “Return To Facts”; soften the jaw.
• Loop back? Use “Switch Chair”.
• “Switch Chair” keeps clarity above heat.
• “Place Chairs” to “Return To Facts”: what loosened?
• I can use “Speak Position” without extra heat.

Give both positions a voice without claiming either is fact.

RITUAL
1. Place Chairs — Place two chairs apart.
2. Speak Position — Speak from your position using first person.
3. Switch Chair — Move and answer as the other position, labelling imagination where knowledge is missing.
4. Return To Facts — Return to your chair and state what changed, what did not, and what real conversation may still be needed.

WIN
✓ The next sentence can carry the boundary without carrying the fight.

• Exhale after “Return To Facts”; soften the jaw.
• Loop back? Use “Switch Chair”.
• “Switch Chair” keeps clarity above heat.
• “Place Chairs” to “Return To Facts”: what loosened?
• I can use “Speak Position” without extra heat.

FORMULA FLOW
Place Chairs → Speak Position → Switch Chair → Return To Facts

PAUSE
Avoid this alone for traumatic relationships or if role-switching feels disorganising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOVE THE CHARGE INTO A CONTAINER
goal: Body alarm needs a route with walls.
steps:
1. Choose Shaking — Choose shaking, pushing a wall, stamping, stretching, or strong walking.
2. Start Define — Define space, duration, and maximum intensity before starting.
3. Keep Movement — Keep movement nonviolent and stop at the timer.
4. Take Earliest Move — Stand still afterward until you notice the earliest settling marker.
win: ✓ Gave the charge a container and stayed long enough to feel it settle.
supports:

• Return once to “Keep Movement”.
• “Keep Movement” proves motion is available.
• “Choose Shaking” versus “Take Earliest Move”: what eased?
• I can use “Start Define” before motivation.

title: MOVE THE HEAVIEST WORD
goal: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
steps:
1. Say Alarm — Choose the exact alarm sentence and shorten it to seven words or fewer.
2. Shift Stress — Say it quietly several times, moving emphasis to one different word per round. Keep pitch and speed comfortable.
3. Find Weight — Notice which emphasis changes the meaning or body response most. Focus only on that word.
4. Keep Signal — Keep the weighted word as information; stop the repetitions without debating the whole sentence.
win: ✓ I found the word carrying the weight and stopped rehearsing the whole sentence.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Keep Signal”; no breath-holding.
• Re-entry move: “Find Weight”.
• “Find Weight” — alarm isn’t command.
• Before/after: “Say Alarm” → “Keep Signal”.
• I can use “Shift Stress” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Say Alarm → Shift Stress → Find Weight → Keep Signal
safety:
PAUSE
Use silent emphasis if speaking is unsafe; stop for voice strain, breathing difficulty, or rising panic.

title: A PLACE FOR THE LOSS
goal: Grief needs a deliberate address in time.
steps:

• Look back: “Choose Object” → “Close Bond”.
• I can use “Say Name” while pain stays real.

title: CHANGE THE OBJECT, MARK THE RELEASE
goal: Let matter carry a decision the mind keeps reopening.
steps:
1. Picture Safe — Picture or select a safe symbol for what you are relinquishing.
2. Choose Transformation — Choose a transformation that fits: fold, seal, store, shred, bury where lawful, or dissolve safely.
3. Name Responsibility — Name what is ending and what responsibility remains.
4. Mark the Release — Complete the physical change once.

• Return once to “Name Responsibility”.

title: CROSS OUT THE EXPIRED FUTURE
goal: A prediction should lose influence when its decision window closes.
steps:

2. Imagine Line — When that condition arrives, imagine a line through the prediction and picture the word EXPIRED.
3. Remove Vote — It may remain historically visible, but it receives no further vote.
win: ✓ The expired future lost its vote.
supports:

• On return: “Imagine Line”.
• “Imagine Line” — fear isn’t fate.
• Before/after: “Picture Prediction” → “Remove Vote”.
• I can use “Imagine Line” while fear stays loud.

TITLE
CROSS OUT THE EXPIRED FUTURE

GOAL
A prediction should lose influence when its decision window closes.

RITUAL
1. Picture Prediction — Picture the prediction and the exact condition that makes it obsolete: date passed, result known, action completed, evidence changed.
2. Imagine Line — When that condition arrives, imagine a line through the prediction and picture the word EXPIRED.
3. Remove Vote — It may remain historically visible, but it receives no further vote.

WIN
✓ The expired future lost its vote.

• Exhale after “Remove Vote”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Imagine Line”.
• “Imagine Line” — fear isn’t fate.
• Before/after: “Picture Prediction” → “Remove Vote”.
• I can use “Imagine Line” while fear stays loud.

FORMULA FLOW
Picture Prediction → Imagine Line → Remove Vote

PAUSE
Reopen only when genuinely new evidence creates a new forecast.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
goal: Grammar can accidentally keep history live.
steps:
1. Use Happened — Retell one short segment using was, happened, had, and then.
2. Ground Between — After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: your present location, the current year, and what choice exists now.
3. Finish Moment — Finish with: ‘That ended; this moment is different.’
win: ✓ The sentence moved the memory back into past tense.
supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Moment”; let feeling settle.
• Return once to “Ground Between”.
• “Ground Between” separates feeling from fact.
• “Finish Moment”: what changed from “Use Happened”?
• I can use “Ground Between” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Use Happened → Ground Between → Finish Moment
safety:
PAUSE
Do not retell alone if the memory overwhelms sense of where you are.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TODAY’S FURTHEST USEFUL HORIZON
goal: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.
steps:
1. Ask Far — Ask how far ahead consequences can meaningfully alter today’s move: tonight, one week, six months.
2. Imagine Line — Imagine a line at that horizon.
3. Park Scenario — Park every scenario beyond it unless it changes a present safety or commitment fact.
4. Decide Information — Decide using information inside the line.
win: ✓ The decision stayed inside today’s useful horizon.
supports:
• Exhale after “Decide Information”; end the lap.
• On return: “Park Scenario”.
• “Park Scenario” proves loops can stop.
• Compare “Ask Far” with “Decide Information”.
• I can use “Imagine Line” without another lap.
formula_flow: Ask Far → Imagine Line → Park Scenario → Decide Information

title: BREAK THE DEADLINE MONOLITH
goal: Time pressure shrinks when it gains windows.
steps:
1. Count Usable — Count the usable work blocks remaining, subtracting sleep and fixed duties.
2. Give Block — Give each block one deliverable with a visible finish.
3. Place Buffers — Place buffers before the final deadline.
4. Start Earliest — Start the earliest window; refuse to mentally carry later windows inside it.
win: ✓ The decision regained enough space to be a decision.
supports:
• Exhale after “Start Earliest”; slow the clock.
• Shortcut: “Place Buffers”, once.
• “Place Buffers” puts facts above speed.
• Before/after: “Count Usable” → “Start Earliest”.
• I can use “Give Block” without rushing.
formula_flow: Count Usable → Give Block → Place Buffers → Start Earliest

title: THE AFTERSHOCK CLOCK
goal: Residual body alarm is not fresh evidence.
steps:
1. Set Reasonable — Set a reasonable after-event window during which shakiness, replay, fatigue, or emotion are expected echoes.
2. Picture Time — Picture its end time.
3. Notice Sensations — Until then, keep sensations but forbid them from changing your meaning of what happened.
4. Reassess — Reassess after recovery and sleep where possible.
win: ✓ I recognised the aftershock as residue, not fresh evidence.
supports:
• Exhale after “Reassess”; then keep moving.
• On return, repeat “Notice Sensations”.
• “Notice Sensations” proves motion is available.
• “Reassess”: what changed from “Set Reasonable”?
• I can use “Picture Time” before motivation.
formula_flow: Set Reasonable → Picture Time → Notice Sensations → Reassess

title: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
goal: Put the real years back between then and now.
steps:
1. Date Events — Picture the dates of the events that currently feel piled together.
2. Scale Distance — Give equal physical space to equal spans of time; do not place every event in one crowded cluster.
3. Present — Notice TODAY at the correct distance and name one fact that belongs only to now.
4. Recheck Urgency — Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored.
win: ✓ Speed stopped masquerading as necessity.
supports:
• Exhale after “Recheck Urgency”; slow the clock.
• If it flares, choose “Present”.
• “Present” puts facts above speed.
• What lost power: “Date Events” → “Recheck Urgency”?
• I can use “Scale Distance” without rushing.
formula_flow: Date Events → Scale Distance → Present → Recheck Urgency

title: TWENTY SECONDS BEFORE THE STORY
goal: Let sensation stay fluid before language freezes it.
steps:
1. Name Causes — For twenty seconds, ban emotion names and causes.
2. Describe Geometry — Say only geometry and physics: shape, temperature, pressure, texture, direction, pulse.
3. Choose Smallest — At the bell, choose the smallest Name that fits, or keep it unnamed if none does.
win: ✓ Sensation stayed fluid long enough to avoid becoming a premature story.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Smallest”; let feeling settle.
• Use “Describe Geometry” on return.
• “Describe Geometry” separates feeling from fact.
• “Name Causes” to “Choose Smallest”: what loosened?
• I can use “Describe Geometry” while emotion stays loud.

title: THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST
goal: Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.
steps:
1. Describe Event — Frame the moment once as ‘this mind is predicting…’ or ‘the system is producing…’.
2. Change — Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
3. Return Person — Then return to first person for the action you really own: ‘I will…’.
4. Loosen the Grammar — Distance the content, not agency.
win: ✓ I loosened the grammar without giving away ownership of the experience.
supports:
• Exhale after “Loosen the Grammar”; end the lap.
• Skip replay; use “Return Person”.
• “Return Person” proves loops can stop.
• Before/after: “Describe Event” → “Loosen the Grammar”.
• I can use “Change” without another lap.
formula_flow: Describe Event → Change → Return Person → Loosen the Grammar

title: LET THE IMAGE FIND ITS LAST FRAME

title: NO-CONCEPT MINUTE
goal: Reality gets one minute without explanation.
steps:
1. Set Brief — Set a brief interval.
2. Name Comparisons — During it, do not create causes, labels, comparisons, or solutions.
3. Attend Direct — Attend to direct colour, sound, contact, and movement.
4. Let Sensory — If a concept appears, acknowledge ‘explanation’ and let the sensory world continue.

• I can use “Name Comparisons” to return here.

title: COOL THE WORDS, KEEP THE FACTS
goal: Language can lower heat without lowering truth.
steps:
1. Underline — Underline absolutes and inflammatory terms in your account.
2. Observe Behaviour — Exchange every one for a precise factual equivalent: ‘always’ becomes the actual frequency; ‘destroyed’ becomes the specific loss; ‘evil’ becomes the observed behaviour.
3. Read Action — Re-read and notice what action the cooler version supports.
win: ✓ The facts stayed; the heat came down.
supports:
• Exhale after “Read Action”; then keep moving.
• If it flares, choose “Observe Behaviour”.
• “Observe Behaviour” proves motion is available.
• “Underline” versus “Read Action”: what eased?
• I can use “Observe Behaviour” before motivation.

title: CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS
goal: Reality’s surprise is premium evidence.
steps:
1. Keep Both Versions — The moment an outcome differs from expectation, keep both versions verbatim.
2. State Size — State the size and direction of the error.
3. Name Miss — Finish with: ‘The old model must now explain…’ and name the discrepancy.
4. Preserve Forecast — Do not let hindsight rewrite the original prediction.
win: ✓ Original prediction preserved. Hindsight cannot edit the miss now.
supports:

• Shortcut: “Name Miss”, once.
• “Name Miss” puts facts above speed.
• “Keep Both Versions” to “Preserve Forecast”: what loosened?
• I can use “State Size” without rushing.

title: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
goal: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
steps:
1. Pin Forecast — Restate the fear as one visible or audible prediction—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Set Clock — Give the prediction a real time window.
3. Score Odds — Set confidence on a 0–100 scale before checking anything.
4. Observe Safely — Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Update Odds — Hold the result and update confidence in either direction.
win: ✓ The next move no longer has to obey the loudest second.
supports:
• Exhale after “Update Odds”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Score Odds”.
• “Observe Safely” — fear isn’t fate.
• What lost power: “Pin Forecast” → “Update Odds”?
• I can use “Set Clock” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Pin Forecast → Set Clock → Score Odds → Observe Safely → Update Odds

title: CONFIDENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE
goal: Certainty and support need separate meters.
steps:

goal: Absence becomes evidence only after prediction says what should be present.
steps:

title: SAME FACTS, THREE ASSUMPTIONS
goal: Stress-test the belief by changing only its hidden premise.
steps:
1. Keep Observations — Keep all observations fixed.
2. Reframe Three Ways — Run the same facts through three different assumptions about motive, capability, or context.
3. Identify Action — For each, spot the one simple action it recommends.
4. Compare Action — Compare which action remains robust across versions.
win: ✓ Three premises produced three worlds; only the robust action survived all of them.
supports:
• Exhale after “Compare Action”; keep both sides.
• On return: “Identify Action”.
• “Identify Action” widens the evidence field.
• What lost power: “Keep Observations” → “Compare Action”?
• I can use “Reframe Three Ways” before concluding.
formula_flow: Keep Observations → Reframe Three Ways → Identify Action → Compare Action

content:
TITLE
SAME FACTS, THREE ASSUMPTIONS

GOAL
Stress-test the belief by changing only its hidden premise.

RITUAL
1. Keep Observations — Keep all observations fixed.
2. Reframe Three Ways — Run the same facts through three different assumptions about motive, capability, or context.
3. Identify Action — For each, spot the one simple action it recommends.
4. Compare Action — Compare which action remains robust across versions.

WIN
✓ Three premises produced three worlds; only the robust action survived all of them.

• Exhale after “Compare Action”; keep both sides.
• On return: “Identify Action”.
• “Identify Action” widens the evidence field.
• What lost power: “Keep Observations” → “Compare Action”?
• I can use “Reframe Three Ways” before concluding.

FORMULA FLOW
Keep Observations → Reframe Three Ways → Identify Action → Compare Action

PAUSE
Avoid invented alternatives that contradict established evidence.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FORECAST WITH A LANDING ZONE
goal: Accuracy can include an honest margin of error.
steps:
1. Predict Range — Predict a range rather than a perfect point.
2. State Acceptable — State the acceptable error band and why it is reasonable.
3. Measure Reality — After the result, measure reality check: inside, near, or outside the band.
4. Widen the Landing — Adjust future range width instead of declaring success or failure.
win: ✓ The forecast became a range, so reality had somewhere honest to land.
supports:
• Exhale after “Widen the Landing”; release the score.
• If it flares, choose “Measure Reality”.
• “Measure Reality” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Widen the Landing”: what changed from “Predict Range”?
• I can use “State Acceptable” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Predict Range → State Acceptable → Measure Reality → Widen the Landing

title: WAIT FOR THE EVIDENCE THAT CAN EXIST
goal: Some decisions are early because their key fact has not been born.
steps:
1. Name Future — Name the future information that could really change the choice, when it becomes available, and how each possible result would alter action.
2. Wait Evidence — Wait only for that evidence.
3. Reject Delay — Everything else is delay wearing a research badge.
win: ✓ I stopped researching a fact that does not exist yet.
supports:
• Exhale after “Reject Delay”; end the lap.
• Return once to “Wait Evidence”.
• “Wait Evidence” proves loops can stop.
• What changed: “Name Future” → “Reject Delay”?
• I can use “Wait Evidence” without another lap.
formula_flow: Name Future → Wait Evidence → Reject Delay
safety:
PAUSE
Act with current information if delay itself creates material risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

goal: Danger loses monopoly when neutral data re-enters vision.
steps:

• “Hold Trigger” → “Let Central”: what changed?
• I can use “Look Away” amid noise.

title: ZOOM LENS TRAINING
goal: Attention needs more than one focal length.
steps:
1. Choose Object — Select an object.
2. Spend — Spend ten seconds on one tiny feature, ten on the object and nearby context, and ten on the whole visual field.
3. Repeat Shift — Repeat in reverse.
4. Select Aperture — Select the aperture that best fits the actual task.
win: ✓ I changed focal length instead of forcing one kind of attention to do every job.
supports:
• Exhale after “Select Aperture”; keep both sides.
• On return, repeat “Repeat Shift”.
• “Repeat Shift” widens the evidence field.
• “Select Aperture”: what changed from “Choose Object”?
• I can use “Spend” before concluding.

goal: Rotate before one cue becomes background noise.
steps:

3. Finish Channel — Finish on the channel that restored the clearest present contact.

• I can use “Switch Getting” to return here.

title: RUN THE TWO-WORD TASK
goal: Focus needs one live command, not the whole project shouting at once.
steps:
1. Scan Work — Look at the task and choose the single action verb needed for the next minute: read, compare, type, sort, call, or check.
2. Pick Verb — Choose the exact object receiving that action: paragraph, invoice, shelf, patient Name, pan, or message.
3. Bind Object — Join them into a two-word command such as TYPE SUMMARY or SORT RECEIPTS. Hide every other instruction for now.
4. Run Command — Run the command for sixty to ninety seconds. Stop only when the verb or object really needs to change.
win: ✓ The task stayed tiny enough to keep moving.
supports:
• One exhale after “Run Command”; redirect attention.
• Return once to “Bind Object”.
• “Bind Object” proves one signal leads.
• “Run Command”: what changed from “Scan Work”?
• I can use “Pick Verb” amid noise.

TITLE
RUN THE TWO-WORD TASK

GOAL
Focus needs one live command, not the whole project shouting at once.

RITUAL
1. Scan Work — Look at the task and choose the single action verb needed for the next minute: read, compare, type, sort, call, or check.
2. Pick Verb — Choose the exact object receiving that action: paragraph, invoice, shelf, patient Name, pan, or message.
3. Bind Object — Join them into a two-word command such as TYPE SUMMARY or SORT RECEIPTS. Hide every other instruction for now.
4. Run Command — Run the command for sixty to ninety seconds. Stop only when the verb or object really needs to change.

WIN
✓ The task stayed tiny enough to keep moving.

• One exhale after “Run Command”; redirect attention.
• Return once to “Bind Object”.
• “Bind Object” proves one signal leads.
• “Run Command”: what changed from “Scan Work”?
• I can use “Pick Verb” amid noise.

Scan Work → Pick Verb → Bind Object → Run Command

title: MEASURE THE EMOTION’S VELOCITY
goal: Intensity is a photograph; momentum is the film.
steps:
1. Set Level — At three intervals, keep not only level but direction and speed: rising fast, steady, falling slowly.
2. Add Action — Add the action impulse at each point.
3. Make Decisions — Make decisions from trajectory plus facts, not from the first intensity number alone.
win: ✓ The feeling became a moving trend, not a frozen number.
supports:
• Exhale after “Make Decisions”; let wanting crest.
• Loop back? Use “Add Action”.
• “Add Action” keeps wanting off controls.

GOAL
Slow the first move enough to catch the launch.

RITUAL
1. Identify Earliest — Catch the first movement linked to the urge—turning, reaching, standing, typing.
2. Observe Direction — do only that movement at half speed while observing its direction and tension.
3. Pause Completion — Pause at completion and decide whether the second movement serves you.

WIN
✓ Slowing the launch exposed the choice before the second move fired.

• Exhale after “Pause Completion”; mark the pause.
• If it flares, choose “Observe Direction”.
• “Observe Direction” proves choice interrupted habit.
• “Pause Completion”: what changed from “Identify Earliest”?
• I can use “Observe Direction” before autopilot.

FORMULA FLOW
Identify Earliest → Observe Direction → Pause Completion

PAUSE
Do not slow a movement needed for immediate safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RETURN EACH LOAD TO ITS SOURCE
goal: One problem should not carry the weight of the whole week.
steps:
1. Estimate Contribution — Name current stressors and estimate each contribution to body alarm.

3. Stop Blaming — Address the largest actionable contributor first; stop blaming the most visible issue for unrelated load.
win: ✓ The week stopped collapsing into one overloaded problem.
supports:
• Exhale after “Stop Blaming”; then keep moving.
• On return, repeat “Imagine Arrows”.
• “Imagine Arrows” proves motion is available.
• “Estimate Contribution” to “Stop Blaming”: what loosened?
• I can use “Imagine Arrows” before motivation.

title: THE EMOTION STOPS AT THE SKIN
goal: Another person’s state is information, not automatic duty.
steps:
1. Emotion — Notice where their emotion seems to enter your body.
2. Trace Physical — Trace your physical boundary with gaze or touch.
3. State Action — State what action is yours, what remains theirs, and what you can offer without taking ownership.
4. Stay Blurred — Adjust distance if the distinction stays blurred.
win: ✓ Their emotion stopped at their skin; my duty stopped there too.
supports:
• Exhale after “Stay Blurred”; release extra load.
• Skip replay; use “State Action”.
• “State Action” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Look back: “Emotion” → “Stay Blurred”.
• I can use “Trace Physical” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Emotion → Trace Physical → State Action → Stay Blurred

content:
TITLE
THE EMOTION STOPS AT THE SKIN

GOAL
Another person’s state is information, not automatic duty.

RITUAL
1. Emotion — Notice where their emotion seems to enter your body.
2. Trace Physical — Trace your physical boundary with gaze or touch.
3. State Action — State what action is yours, what remains theirs, and what you can offer without taking ownership.
4. Stay Blurred — Adjust distance if the distinction stays blurred.

WIN
✓ Their emotion stopped at their skin; my duty stopped there too.

• Exhale after “Stay Blurred”; release extra load.
• Skip replay; use “State Action”.
• “State Action” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Look back: “Emotion” → “Stay Blurred”.
• I can use “Trace Physical” without carrying it all.

FORMULA FLOW
Emotion → Trace Physical → State Action → Stay Blurred

PAUSE
Honour mandated or genuine care responsibilities rather than withdrawing reflexively.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
goal: Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.
steps:
1. Press Equal — Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Match Force — Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Step Down — Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach Zero — Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns.
win: ✓ I matched the pressure, brought it back to zero, and checked what remained.
supports:
• Exhale after “Reach Zero”; mark the pause.
• If it flares, choose “Step Down”.
• “Step Down” proves choice interrupted habit.
• What lost power: “Press Equal” → “Reach Zero”?
• I can use “Match Force” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Press Equal → Match Force → Step Down → Reach Zero
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid this with pain, hand or joint injury, numbness, breath holding, or any unsafe physical symptom.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PIN A RETURN ADDRESS
goal: A distraction should cost one return address, not a full reconstruction.
steps:
1. Name Object — Name the exact OBJECT currently carrying the task: document, pan, form, email, shelf, or tool.
2. Place — Notice the precise LOCATION inside it: paragraph three, top-left field, second burner, or blue tab.
3. Choose Verb — Choose one NEXT VERB for that location: compare, type, turn, check, send, or place.
4. Reenter — After the interruption, say the three-part address once and act on the verb without rescanning the entire task.
win: ✓ Autopilot missed its usual handoff.
supports:
• Exhale after “Reenter”; mark the pause.
• On return, repeat “Choose Verb”.
• “Choose Verb” proves choice interrupted habit.
• “Reenter”: what changed from “Name Object”?
• I can use “Place” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Name Object → Place → Choose Verb → Reenter

title: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
goal: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.
steps:
1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.
win: ✓ The alarm panel stopped behaving like one fused signal.
supports:
• Exhale after “Check Panel”; then keep moving.
• Return once to “Move Dial”.
• “Move Dial” proves motion is available.
• At “Check Panel”, compare “Read Channels”.
• I can use “Pick Smallest” before motivation.
formula_flow: Read Channels → Pick Smallest → Move Dial → Check Panel

DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL

GOAL
The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.

RITUAL
1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.

WIN
✓ The alarm panel stopped behaving like one fused signal.

• Exhale after “Check Panel”; then keep moving.
• Return once to “Move Dial”.
• “Move Dial” proves motion is available.
• At “Check Panel”, compare “Read Channels”.
• I can use “Pick Smallest” before motivation.

FORMULA FLOW
Read Channels → Pick Smallest → Move Dial → Check Panel

PAUSE
New, severe, or unusual physical symptoms require medical assessment. Stop for pain, faintness, breathing difficulty, confusion, or loss of orientation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHANGE THE RHYTHM, CHANGE THE STATE
goal: Emotion maintains itself through tempo as well as story.
steps:
1. Cadence — Notice the cadence of speech, movement, or breathing.
2. Choose Opposite — Choose an opposite rhythm: agitated becomes deliberate, collapsed becomes lightly brisk, looping becomes irregular.
3. Observe Emotional — Maintain the new tempo through one simple task and observe the emotional shift.
win: ✓ I changed the tempo and gave the state a different rhythm to follow.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Observe Emotional”; no breath-holding.
• If it flares, choose “Choose Opposite”.
• “Choose Opposite” — alarm isn’t command.
• Before/after: “Cadence” → “Observe Emotional”.
• I can use “Choose Opposite” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Cadence → Choose Opposite → Observe Emotional

title: FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY
goal: Inner agreement is optional; a move that betrays no red line is enough.
steps:
1. Seat Feelings — Label up to three active emotions as players at the table. Leave them unnamed for the moment; observe first.
2. Vetoes — Give each emotion one veto: ‘Fear will not accept ___. Anger will not accept ___. Sadness will not accept ___.’
3. Clear Board — Cross out actions blocked by any safe, reasonable veto. Ignore demands for harm, punishment, or impossible certainty. Put it into simple words a child could understand.
4. Choose Survivor — Choose one remaining action that crosses no red line, even if no feeling loves it.
win: ✓ No feeling agreed, but no red line had to be betrayed.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Survivor”; soften the jaw.
• Shortcut: “Clear Board”, once.
• “Clear Board” keeps clarity above heat.
• Difference check: “Seat Feelings” → “Choose Survivor”.
• I can use “Vetoes” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Seat Feelings → Vetoes → Clear Board → Choose Survivor
safety:
PAUSE
Safety, consent, law, and basic care outrank every emotional veto; seek support if no safe move remains.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GLOBAL LABELS NEED THREE RECEIPTS
goal: Identity claims must show recent action evidence.
steps:
1. Name Appears — When ‘I’m lazy,’ ‘I’m unlovable,’ or another global Name appears, demand three specific behaviours from the last month that support it and three that complicate it.
2. Replace Identity — If the evidence is mixed, replace identity with a narrower situational description.
win: ✓ The global label could not produce three clean receipts.
supports:
• Exhale after “Replace Identity”; loosen the label.
• Pulled back? Touch “Replace Identity”.
• “Name Appears” — the rule loosened.
• Difference check: “Name Appears” → “Replace Identity”.
• I can use “Replace Identity” without becoming the label.

steps:

• Catch restart with “Design Alternative”.
• “Design Alternative” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• “Test Low”: what changed from “Choose Disliked”?
• I can use “Ask Threat” without ranking my worth.

title: REMOVE THE AUDIENCE
goal: Find the choice that survives without witnesses.
steps:
1. Imagine Nobody — Imagine nobody will see, praise, criticise, repost, or hear about the action.
2. Erase Audience — Erase the imagined audience one row at a time.
3. Choose Direct — What would you choose if only direct consequences and values remained?
4. Take Smallest — Take the smallest version privately.
win: ✓ Loss did not erase every direction.
supports:
• Exhale after “Take Smallest”; keep the compass.
• If it flares, choose “Choose Direct”.
• “Choose Direct” keeps meaning in motion.
• Keep one lesson: “Imagine Nobody” → “Take Smallest”.
• I can use “Erase Audience” while pain stays real.

title: BLANK THE NAMEPLATE
goal: Cover the label and see what you choose without it.
steps:
1. Picture Identity — Picture the identity label on a removable card and turn it face down.
2. Decision — For the next decision, refer only to capacities, needs, facts, and values.

win: ✓ The label went dark. The choice still appeared.
supports:
• Exhale after “Uncover Name”; loosen the label.
• Pulled back? Touch “Choose Shift”.
• “Choose Shift” — the rule loosened.
• What lost power: “Picture Identity” → “Uncover Name”?
• I can use “Decision” without becoming the label.

title: CALL THE INNER COUNCIL
goal: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
steps:
1. Give Self — Give each self-state a seat.
2. Sentence — One sentence each: what I need, what I fear, what I propose.
3. Protect Whole — Appoint a chair whose job is to protect the whole system over time.
4. Chair the Council — The chair may combine, delay, or reject proposals, but must acknowledge every need.
win: ✓ Every inner voice got heard; none got automatic control.
supports:
• Exhale after “Chair the Council”; end the lap.
• Loop back? Use “Protect Whole”.
• “Protect Whole” proves loops can stop.
• “Give Self” versus “Chair the Council”: what eased?
• I can use “Sentence” without another lap.
formula_flow: Give Self → Sentence → Protect Whole → Chair the Council

title: EXIST FOR ONE MINUTE WITHOUT AUTOBIOGRAPHY
goal: Ongoing sense can be sensed before the life story is consulted.
steps:
1. Don't Recall — For sixty seconds, do not recall name, history, status, or plans.
2. Stay Changing — Stay with changing sound, pressure, light, and movement.
3. Simple — Notice the simple ongoing sense of being present through those changes.
4. End Reclaim — Reclaim your biography on purpose at the end.
win: ✓ For one minute, existence did not need a biography.
supports:
• Exhale after “End Reclaim”; loosen the label.
• On return, repeat “Simple”.
• “Simple” — the rule loosened.
• “Don't Recall” → “End Reclaim”: what changed?
• I can use “Stay Changing” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Don't Recall → Stay Changing → Simple → End Reclaim
safety:

title: MOVE THE MEMORY CAMERA
goal: You can preserve facts without re-entering the old viewpoint.
steps:
1. Place Memory — Place the memory on a screen with enough visual distance.
2. View Scene — View the scene from above, behind, or beside a compassionate observer.
3. Keep Events — Keep events accurate while changing camera position.
4. Add Resources — Add current-you outside the frame with present resources.
win: ✓ The memory camera moved, and the present kept its own frame.
supports:
• Exhale after “Add Resources”; drop the scoreboard.
• Loop back? Use “Keep Events”.
• “Keep Events” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• What lost power: “Place Memory” → “Add Resources”?
• I can use “View Scene” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Place Memory → View Scene → Keep Events → Add Resources

title: THE MEMORY DOES NOT END THERE
goal: Pain may be stored without its later survival chapter.

4. Restore — Restore the omitted chronology.

• What lost power: “End Retell” → “Restore”?

title: TURN DOWN THE DOMINANT CHANNEL
goal: A memory can feel present because one sense owns the mix.
steps:
1. Identify Loudest — Spot the loudest recall channel—image, sound, touch, smell.
2. Reduce Brightness — Reduce its brightness, volume, proximity, or texture slightly.
3. Anchor the Present — At the same time, strengthen neutral present-day context: the room layout, today’s date, your clothing, or a distant sound.
win: ✓ Memory lost the whole screen; the present regained channels.
supports:
• Exhale after “Anchor the Present”; keep both sides.
• Skip replay; use “Reduce Brightness”.
• “Reduce Brightness” widens the evidence field.
• “Anchor the Present”: what changed from “Identify Loudest”?
• I can use “Reduce Brightness” before concluding.
formula_flow: Identify Loudest → Reduce Brightness → Anchor the Present

title: POWER THEN, RESOURCES NOW
goal: Past helplessness should not inherit present equipment.
steps:
1. Imagine Two Sides — Imagine two sides.
2. Then — On the first side, picture your age, knowledge, money, power, support, and choices then.
3. Picture Today — On the second side, picture the same things today.
4. Find The Change — Notice what gives you more choice now.
5. Use One Resource — Pick one resource you have today and use it in one small action.
win: ✓ The past kept its history; today’s resources entered the scene.
supports:
• Exhale after “Use One Resource”; end the lap.
• Re-entry move: “Picture Today”.
• “Find The Change” proves loops can stop.
• Before/after: “Imagine Two Sides” → “Use One Resource”.
• I can use “Then” without another lap.

title: RETURN THEIR ACTION; KEEP YOUR CHOICE
goal: What someone did is not your identity property.
steps:

2. Keep Each Part — Keep each thought in the right box.
3. Skip Forced Forgiveness — Forgiveness is not required on command.
4. Act From Choice — Take one action from the third box.
win: ✓ The surge has a shape now instead of filling everything.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Act From Choice”; no breath-holding.
• On return: “Skip Forced Forgiveness”.

• Look back: “Imagine Three Boxes” → “Act From Choice”.
• I can use “Keep Each Part” while alarm rises.

title: ADD THE WITNESS WHO SHOULD HAVE BEEN THERE
goal: The remembered self deserves credible rethought.
steps:

win: ✓ The missing witness finally sounded believable, not magical.

• Catch restart with “Name Wrong”.
• “Name Wrong” proves thought is observable.

TITLE

GOAL
The memory can submit one claim without replaying the entire case.

RITUAL
1. Headline Event — State the event as one factual headline with no motive and no sensory replay.
2. Extract Claim — Finish this sentence once: ‘This memory still seems to demand ___.’ Keep only one claim.
3. Route Bill — Route the claim to BOUNDARY, REPAIR, GRIEF, or IMPOSSIBLE REVERSAL. Do not create a fifth category.
4. Act Present — Choose the matching present response: set protection, request safe repair, make room for grief, or stop billing today for a reversal history cannot provide.

WIN
✓ The old bill met today’s receipt—and stopped charging the present.

• Exhale after “Act Present”; end the lap.
• Skip replay; use “Route Bill”.
• “Route Bill” proves loops can stop.
• “Headline Event” → “Act Present”: what changed?
• I can use “Extract Claim” without another lap.

FORMULA FLOW
Headline Event → Extract Claim → Route Bill → Act Present

PAUSE
Do not contact unsafe people, seek revenge, force reconciliation, or use this game during trauma flooding or immediate danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SAVE THE LESSON, DELETE THE VERDICT
goal: A useful warning does not require a ruined identity or world.
steps:

2. Spot Verdict — Notice the global conclusion attached to it: ‘Nobody is safe,’ ‘I am weak,’ ‘Life is over,’ or another all-life verdict.

• Restart detected: “Spot Verdict”.

• I can use “Spot Verdict” before concluding.

title: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
goal: When the doorway is the problem, let chance choose a safe entrance.
steps:
1. Number Doors — Name three to six task sections that can safely be done in any order and give each one a number.
2. Let Chance Choose — Use a random-number tool on your phone to choose one number. Do not pick again just because you dislike the number.
3. Enter There — Work only inside that section for ninety seconds; do not reorganise the whole project.
4. Mark Progress — Notice one concrete sign of progress, then decide whether to choose another number or close.
win: ✓ A random door beat the perfect doorway.
supports:
• Exhale after “Mark Progress”; release extra blame.
• Skip replay; use “Enter There”.
• “Enter There” keeps blame in proportion.
• Difference check: “Number Doors” → “Mark Progress”.
• I can use “Let Chance Choose” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Number Doors → Let Chance Choose → Enter There → Mark Progress
safety:
PAUSE
Use this only for reorderable work; never randomise required safety, medical, legal, financial, or technical sequences.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

content:
TITLE
MATCH THE TASK TO THE BODY’S TEMPERATURE

GOAL
Action fails when stimulation and state are badly paired.

RITUAL
1. Read Body — Read current body alarm as lower, middle, or high.
2. Select Work — Select work with matching demand: energising movement for low, steady production for medium, simple contained tasks for high.
3. Reassess — Reassess after one unit and change lanes if needed.

WIN
✓ I matched the task to the body I actually had today.

• One exhale after “Reassess”; keep moving.
• Restart detected: “Select Work”.
• “Select Work” proves motion is available.
• Before/after: “Read Body” → “Reassess”.
• I can use “Select Work” before motivation.

FORMULA FLOW
Read Body → Select Work → Reassess

PAUSE
Do not treat serious fatigue or agitation as a productivity puzzle.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ENTER THROUGH THE SIDE DOOR
goal: Resistance may accept a neighbouring move.
steps:
1. Choose Side Door — Pick a small action beside the main task: open one file before starting the work, put on walking shoes before deciding to walk, or wash one ingredient before cooking.
2. Let It Lead — Start with that small step and let it naturally lead into the main task.
win: ✓ Accountability stayed; self-punishment lost ground.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let It Lead”; release extra blame.
• On return, repeat “Let It Lead”.
• “Choose Side Door” keeps blame in proportion.
• “Choose Side Door” → “Let It Lead”: what changed?
• I can use “Let It Lead” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Choose Side Door → Let It Lead

title: THE VERSION THAT STILL COUNTS
goal: Perfection should not be allowed to cancel function.
steps:
1. Name Task — Name the task’s essential purpose.
2. Remove Feature — Remove every feature not required for that purpose.
3. Build Smallest — Build the smallest deliverable that still works, submit or finish it, then upgrade only if time and value justify the addition.
win: ✓ I built the smallest version that still counted, finished it, and left upgrades optional.
supports:
• Exhale after “Build Smallest”; release the score.
• Shortcut: “Remove Feature”, once.
• “Remove Feature” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• Before/after: “Name Task” → “Build Smallest”.
• I can use “Remove Feature” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Name Task → Remove Feature → Build Smallest
safety:
PAUSE
Maintain full standards for safety-critical, clinical, legal, or hard to undo work.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SET THE LIMIT BEFORE THE NEXT TEST
goal: Decide the enforcement rule while the room is calm.
steps:
1. Count Pattern — Define the behaviour in terms a camera could Keep.
2. Set Threshold — Choose the count, duration, or date that will Notice the limit.
3. Link Consequence — Attach one consequence under your control, such as ending the call, leaving, or changing access.
4. Follow Contract — If the threshold is crossed, follow the contract once without holding a motive trial.
win: ✓ The boundary was decided in calm, so motive did not get a retrial.
supports:
• Exhale after “Follow Contract”; release extra load.
• On return: “Link Consequence”.
• “Link Consequence” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Difference check: “Count Pattern” → “Follow Contract”.
• I can use “Set Threshold” without carrying it all.

title: COME BACK FROM THEIR IMAGINED HEAD
goal: Attention belongs first to what can be known.
steps:
1. Sort Three Boxes — Picture three boxes: KNOWN, INFERRED, UNKNOWABLE.
2. Move Claim — Move every claim about the other person into its correct box.
3. Choose Direct — Choose one direct question or boundary based on known facts.
4. Leave Unknowable — Leave the unknowable box empty of action.
win: ✓ What I know became actionable; what I cannot know stayed empty.
supports:
• Exhale after “Leave Unknowable”; release extra load.
• Skip replay; use “Choose Direct”.
• “Choose Direct” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• What lost power: “Sort Three Boxes” → “Leave Unknowable”?
• I can use “Move Claim” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Sort Three Boxes → Move Claim → Choose Direct → Leave Unknowable

title: UNDERSTAND, THEN DISAGREE CLEANLY
goal: Empathy does not sign their conclusion.
steps:
1. View They — Summarise their view until they could recognise it.
2. Name Need — Name the need or logic you understand.
3. Say Meaning — Then say exactly where your meaning, value, or decision differs.
4. Receive Own — No ‘but’ inside the summary; disagreement receives its own sentence.
win: ✓ I understood their view without signing their conclusion.
supports:
• Exhale after “Receive Own”; let feeling settle.
• On return, repeat “Say Meaning”.
• “Say Meaning” separates feeling from fact.
• “View They” versus “Receive Own”: what eased?
• I can use “Name Need” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: View They → Name Need → Say Meaning → Receive Own

title: ONE FIGHT, THREE TIME SCALES
goal: Today’s argument should not impersonate the whole relationship.
steps:
1. Issue Recurring — Check the immediate issue, the recurring pattern, and the full relationship history separately.
2. Give Own — Give each its own conclusion and action. Say what happened as if you were reporting it.
3. Don't Erase — Do not let a good history erase a harmful pattern or one incident erase all context.
win: ✓ One fight found its proper scale—without erasing the history or excusing the pattern.
supports:
• Exhale after “Don't Erase”; soften the jaw.
• Skip replay; use “Give Own”.
• “Give Own” keeps clarity above heat.
• Difference check: “Issue Recurring” → “Don't Erase”.
• I can use “Give Own” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Issue Recurring → Give Own → Don't Erase

title: MAP THE RELATIONSHIP LABOUR
goal: Imbalance becomes negotiable after it becomes visible.
steps:
1. Plan Carries — Across a defined period, tally who initiates, accommodates, repairs, plans, and carries emotional follow-up.
2. Add Context — Include background for genuine capacity differences.
3. Use Categories — Discuss the pattern using categories, not accusations, and request one clear rebalance.
win: ✓ The invisible relationship labour became visible enough to negotiate.

• Catch restart with “Add Context”.

• “Plan Carries” versus “Use Categories”: what eased?
• I can use “Add Context” before concluding.

title: ASK THE QUESTION FEAR KEEPS ANSWERING
goal: Direct data can update the relationship model.
steps:
1. Picture Assumption — Picture the assumption driving your reaction.
2. Question Whose — Convert it into one clear, non-leading question whose answer could prove the assumption wrong.
3. Ask Suitable — Ask at a suitable time, listen fully, and compare reply plus later behaviour with the original model.
win: ✓ Fear finally answered the question it had been answering for me.
supports:
• Exhale after “Ask Suitable”; soften the jaw.
• Shortcut: “Question Whose”, once.
• “Question Whose” keeps clarity above heat.
• “Picture Assumption” to “Ask Suitable”: what loosened?
• I can use “Question Whose” without extra heat.

title: POSTURE WITHOUT PROPHECY
goal: The body can stop rehearsing defeat before facts arrive.
steps:
1. Adopt — Take a stable, non-defensive position: feet supported, spine available, gaze level, arms unguarded enough for safety.
2. Refuse Prophecy — Do not use the posture to predict success or failure.
3. Hold for Evidence — Keep the posture while you wait for actual evidence.
win: ✓ Posture held steady while prophecy waited outside.
supports:
• Exhale after “Hold for Evidence”; then keep moving.
• Loop back? Use “Refuse Prophecy”.
• “Refuse Prophecy” proves motion is available.
• What lost power: “Adopt” → “Hold for Evidence”?
• I can use “Refuse Prophecy” before motivation.

title: SOFT JAW, SAME BOUNDARY
goal: Reduce aggression preparation without weakening the sentence.
steps:
1. Notice Jaw — Notice jaw pressure before speaking.
2. Separate Teeth — Separate the teeth, relax the tongue, and exhale naturally.
3. Deliver Limit — Deliver the exact limit you planned—no extra smile, apology, or attack.
4. Let Articulation — Let articulation stay clear while muscular threat signalling drops.
win: ✓ The boundary kept its strength after the body dropped the threat pose.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Articulation”; release extra load.
• On return, repeat “Deliver Limit”.
• “Deliver Limit” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• At “Let Articulation”, compare “Notice Jaw”.
• I can use “Separate Teeth” without carrying it all.

• “Widen Feet” versus “Observe Shape”: what eased?
• I can use “Keep Change” while alarm rises.

title: LET THE SHAKE BE SMALL
goal: Trembling is movement, not automatic evidence of collapse.
steps:
1. Medically — If medically safe and oriented, permit a small tremor rather than clamping it down.
2. Track Location — Track its location, rhythm, and whether choice remains intact.
3. Let Migrate — Let it stop, continue, or migrate without exaggeration.
4. Let Shake Finish — Ground when the movement ends.
win: ✓ The shake stayed small enough to finish being a shake.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Let Shake Finish”; no breath-holding.
• On return, repeat “Let Migrate”.
• “Let Migrate” — alarm isn’t command.
• Keep one lesson: “Medically” → “Let Shake Finish”.
• I can use “Track Location” while alarm rises.

title: UNWIND IN REVERSE
goal: Release the body by retracing its body alarm order backward.
steps:
1. Recall Muscle — Recall which muscle group tightened last.
2. Soften Work — Soften it first, then work back toward the first area that braced.
3. Pause Handoff — Pause between groups to feel the handoff.
4. Finish Original — Finish at the original starting point and compare the whole chain.
win: ✓ Retracing the alarm backward taught the body how to unwind forward.
supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Original”; mark the pause.
• Restart detected: “Pause Handoff”.
• “Pause Handoff” proves choice interrupted habit.
• Keep one lesson: “Recall Muscle” → “Finish Original”.
• I can use “Soften Work” before autopilot.

title: FINISH THE BODY'S FULL STOP
goal: Let leftover readiness complete one harmless ending.
steps:
1. Find Readiness — While safely seated, locate one area that still feels ready to push, brace, turn, or withdraw.
2. Add Resistance — Choose a pain-free direction and add only light self-resistance.
3. Complete Slowly — Complete the movement slowly once, then release all effort rather than repeating it.
4. Check Neutral — Compare resting pressure, movement range, and urge before and after.
win: ✓ Leftover readiness completed its harmless ending and stopped asking for more.

• Before/after: “Find Readiness” → “Check Neutral”.
• I can use “Add Resistance” before autopilot.

title: BORROW STILLNESS FROM THE WALL
goal: Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.
steps:
1. Rest Gaze — Rest your gaze on a stable line, corner, or heavy object.
2. Compare Visual — Compare its visual constancy with the motion inside your body and mind.
3. Don't Match — Do not make the inner movement match.
4. Let Facts — Let both facts coexist until the outer reference becomes usable.
win: ✓ Stillness entered the scene, so movement stopped being the whole field.

title: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE
goal: Urgency shrinks when hearing regains depth.
steps:
1. Identify Nearest — Spot the nearest sound, one mid-distance sound, and the farthest audible layer.
2. Move Attention — Move attention outward through those distances, then back once.
3. Let Far — Let the far sound widen the perceived space around the closest one.
win: ✓ Distance came back into hearing, and urgency got smaller.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Far”; slow the clock.
• Loop back? Use “Move Attention”.
• “Move Attention” puts facts above speed.
• Difference check: “Identify Nearest” → “Let Far”.
• I can use “Move Attention” without rushing.
formula_flow: Identify Nearest → Move Attention → Let Far

TITLE
SCENT THE RETURN

GOAL
Train one neutral aroma to accompany successful orientation within the current setting.

RITUAL
1. Choose Safe — Take a mild, distinctive scent that feels safe.
2. Use After — Apply it only after you have really returned to present time and choice.
3. Date Grounding — Pair it with date, place, and one grounding action across several occasions.
4. Test Whether — Later, test whether the scent helps retrieve that state.

WIN
✓ I paired one neutral scent with the route back to the present.

• Exhale after “Test Whether”; notice the room.
• On return: “Date Grounding”.
• “Date Grounding” proves the present returned.
• What changed: “Choose Safe” → “Test Whether”?
• I can use “Use After” to return here.

• “Predict Fact”: what changed from “State Fear”?

title: THE ROOM HAS JOBS, NOT DEMANDS
goal: A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.
steps:
1. Scan Objects — Choose four safe visible objects without moving toward them. Avoid screens if they add strain.
2. Name Jobs — For each object, name only its ordinary job: chair supports, lamp lights, cup holds, door opens.
3. Drop Demands — Say ‘not needed now’ to every function that does not serve the current safe moment. Do not remove or organise anything.
4. Choose Helper — Choose the one object whose real function supports what you can do now, then use only that function.
win: ✓ The room went back to having jobs instead of demands.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Helper”; release extra blame.

title: ONE ACTIVE SLOT
goal: Short-term attention needs a deliberate admission policy.
steps:
1. Create Positions — Create three positions: ACTIVE, WAITING, ARCHIVE.
2. Wait Route — Put only one concern in active, one likely next item in waiting, and route everything else to archive with a retrieval Notice.
3. Give Active — Give the active concern a protected time box.
win: ✓ Attention admitted one concern and gave the rest a booked return time.
supports:
• Exhale after “Give Active”; mark the pause.
• Restart detected: “Wait Route”.
• “Wait Route” proves choice interrupted habit.
• “Create Positions” → “Give Active”: what changed?
• I can use “Wait Route” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Create Positions → Wait Route → Give Active

title: HIDE THE OPTION NAMES
goal: See what the options look like before their names start campaigning.
steps:
1. Mask Names — Ask someone—or a shuffled note—to rename the leading options A, B and C without showing which is which.
2. Choose Traits — Choose three relevant traits, such as cost, time, fit, reliability, or learning. Keep safety facts visible.
3. Rank Blind — Compare the symbols on those traits without guessing their identities and hold the current order.
4. Reveal Options — Reveal the names. Keep the blind order or name exactly what changed it and why.
win: ✓ The options lost their campaign slogans; the traits made the first vote.
supports:
• Exhale after “Reveal Options”; drop the scoreboard.
• Re-entry move: “Rank Blind”.
• “Rank Blind” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Compare “Mask Names” with “Reveal Options”.
• I can use “Choose Traits” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Mask Names → Choose Traits → Rank Blind → Reveal Options
safety:
PAUSE
Never hide facts required for safety, consent, ethics, affordability, or professional decision support.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GROUP BY BRAIN MODE
goal: Context switching charges a restart fee.
steps:

title: WHEN DOES THIS INFORMATION EXPIRE?
goal: Data should not remain active after its conditions disappear.
steps:
1. Picture Expiry — For each influential input, picture an expiry condition: price changes, role ends, policy updates, health status shifts, deadline passes.
2. Expire Old Data — Notice any expired item. Stop letting it guide new behaviour until the information is refreshed.
win: ✓ Expired information lost its voting rights until it earns an update.

• I can use “Expire Old Data” before autopilot.

title: SEPARATE THE MENTAL INBOXES
goal: Ideas, duties, fears, and memories should not share one queue.
steps:
1. Question Capture — Catch each mental item, then route it into IDEA, OBLIGATION, FEAR, MEMORY, or QUESTION.
2. Give Category — Give each category its own processing rule.
3. Don't Determine — Prioritise only after sorting, so emotional intensity does not determine inbox order.
win: ✓ The mind got separate queues instead of one emergency pile.

• Shortcut: “Give Category”, once.
• “Give Category” proves choice interrupted habit.
• What changed: “Question Capture” → “Don't Determine”?
• I can use “Give Category” before autopilot.

TITLE

GOAL
Ideas, duties, fears, and memories should not share one queue.

RITUAL
1. Question Capture — Catch each mental item, then route it into IDEA, OBLIGATION, FEAR, MEMORY, or QUESTION.
2. Give Category — Give each category its own processing rule.
3. Don't Determine — Prioritise only after sorting, so emotional intensity does not determine inbox order.

WIN
✓ The mind got separate queues instead of one emergency pile.

• Exhale after “Don't Determine”; mark the pause.
• Shortcut: “Give Category”, once.
• “Give Category” proves choice interrupted habit.
• What changed: “Question Capture” → “Don't Determine”?
• I can use “Give Category” before autopilot.

FORMULA FLOW
Question Capture → Give Category → Don't Determine

PAUSE
Add categories sparingly; excessive sorting can become avoidance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOVE BEFORE MOTIVATION
goal: Feeling ready is not a legal requirement for the first motion.
steps:
1. Begin Anyway — State honestly: ‘Motivation may stay absent.’ Begin the earliest physical component anyway—stand, open, carry, type, dial.
2. Complete Unit — Continue only through one contained unit.
3. Test Momentum — Let action provide data about if further movement is available.
win: ✓ Action produced data before motivation arrived.
supports:
• Exhale after “Test Momentum”; let feeling settle.
• On return, repeat “Complete Unit”.
• “Complete Unit” separates feeling from fact.
• Keep one lesson: “Begin Anyway” → “Test Momentum”.
• I can use “Complete Unit” while emotion stays loud.

title: WHAT KIND OF EFFORT IS THIS?

steps:

• “Stop Novelty” proves thought is observable.
• “Use Evidence” → “Respond Category”: what changed?
• I can use “Stop Novelty” without obeying thought.

title: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
goal: Motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure.
steps:
1. Run Pulse — Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Full Stop — Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Read Strain — Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Set Gear — Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.
win: ✓ One work pulse found the gear motivation could only guess at.
supports:
• Exhale after “Set Gear”; release extra blame.
• Loop back? Use “Read Strain”.
• “Read Strain” keeps blame in proportion.
• At “Set Gear”, compare “Run Pulse”.
• I can use “Full Stop” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Run Pulse → Full Stop → Read Strain → Set Gear
safety:
PAUSE
Stop for pain, illness, exhaustion, agitation, compulsive timing, or any task where interruptions create safety risk.

title: WHAT SPECIES OF UNKNOWN IS THIS?
goal: Different uncertainties require different responses.
steps:

2. Apply Move — Apply its matching move—research, schedule, act on influence, or practise acceptance.
3. Use Category — Refuse to use one category’s tool on another.
win: ✓ The unknown got a species name—and finally received the right tool.

• Loop back? Use “Apply Move”.
• “Apply Move” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• Look back: “Classify” → “Use Category”.
• I can use “Apply Move” without a guarantee.

steps:

2. Place Each Part — Put each piece of the problem in the right ring in your mind.
3. Take Action — Do one thing you control, make one request where you have influence, and let go of one thing you can only watch.

• On return, repeat “Place Each Part”.
• “Place Each Part” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• Difference check: “Imagine Three Rings” → “Take Action”.
• I can use “Place Each Part” without a guarantee.

content:
TITLE
THREE RINGS OF AGENCY

GOAL
Do not spend control effort in the observation ring.

RITUAL
1. Imagine Three Rings — Imagine three rings: CONTROL, INFLUENCE, WATCH.
2. Place Each Part — Put each piece of the problem in the right ring in your mind.
3. Take Action — Do one thing you control, make one request where you have influence, and let go of one thing you can only watch.

WIN
✓ I acted in one ring, asked in one ring, and stopped fighting the third.

• Exhale after “Take Action”; leave it unanswered.
• On return, repeat “Place Each Part”.
• “Place Each Part” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• Difference check: “Imagine Three Rings” → “Take Action”.
• I can use “Place Each Part” without a guarantee.

FORMULA FLOW
Imagine Three Rings → Place Each Part → Take Action

PAUSE
Observation still requires protective action when risk indicators appear.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE UNANSWERED URGE EXPERIMENT
goal: Extra certainty can wait while its appetite changes.
steps:
1. Question Demands — When the question demands an answer, picture it and delay asking for a short, chosen interval.
2. Track Urge — Track urge intensity at beginning, middle, and end without researching.
3. Decide Afterward — Decide afterward whether information is still needed for action or only for relief.
win: ✓ The urge for certainty changed before another answer was purchased.
supports:

• Restart detected: “Track Urge”.
• “Track Urge” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• Look back: “Question Demands” → “Decide Afterward”.
• I can use “Track Urge” without a guarantee.

title: POSSIBLE IS NOT PROBABLE
goal: Separate existence from likelihood and support.
steps:
1. State Lines — State three lines: It is possible that…; It is probable that…; The evidence currently supports….
2. Don't Allow — Do not allow content to migrate upward without justification.
3. Plan Probability — Base planning on chance and safety margin, not possibility alone.
win: ✓ Possible and probable finally stopped sharing a name tag.
supports:
• Exhale after “Plan Probability”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Don't Allow”.
• “Don't Allow” — fear isn’t fate.
• Look back: “State Lines” → “Plan Probability”.
• I can use “Don't Allow” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: State Lines → Don't Allow → Plan Probability
