POSSIBLE IS NOT PROBABLE

GOAL
Separate existence from likelihood and support.

RITUAL
1. State Lines — State three lines: It is possible that…; It is probable that…; The evidence currently supports….
2. Don't Allow — Do not allow content to migrate upward without justification.
3. Plan Probability — Base planning on chance and safety margin, not possibility alone.

WIN
✓ Possible and probable finally stopped sharing a name tag.

• Exhale after “Plan Probability”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Don't Allow”.
• “Don't Allow” — fear isn’t fate.
• Look back: “State Lines” → “Plan Probability”.
• I can use “Don't Allow” while fear stays loud.

FORMULA FLOW
State Lines → Don't Allow → Plan Probability

PAUSE
Low-probability high-impact risks may still justify proportionate precautions.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PLAN BOTH BRANCHES
goal: Uncertainty need not prevent preparation.
steps:
1. Choose Plausible — Choose two plausible outcomes and build a short branch for each: first signal, first action, resource, and exit.
2. Prepare Both — Prepare any step useful in both branches now.
3. Select Path — Delay preference until evidence selects the path.
win: ✓ Both futures got a plan before either one earned belief.
supports:
• Exhale after “Select Path”; leave it unanswered.
• Re-entry move: “Prepare Both”.
• “Prepare Both” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Choose Plausible” to “Select Path”: what loosened?
• I can use “Prepare Both” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Choose Plausible → Prepare Both → Select Path

title: SWAP OUTCOME CONTROL FOR PROCESS CONTROL
goal: Measure what your hands can actually influence.
steps:
1. Name Desired — Name the desired outcome and cross it out as the score.
2. Practise Applications — Substitute one visible process variable fully under your control—calls made, honest minutes practised, applications sent, boundary delivered.
3. Score the Process — Check success only on that variable for the chosen period.
win: ✓ Success moved onto the part my hands can actually control.
supports:
• Exhale after “Score the Process”; leave it unanswered.
• Catch restart with “Practise Applications”.
• “Practise Applications” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Score the Process”: what changed from “Name Desired”?
• I can use “Practise Applications” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Name Desired → Practise Applications → Score the Process

title: THREE INCOMPATIBLE READINGS
goal: Uncertainty is not evidence for your favourite meaning.
steps:

2. Identify Future — Generate three explanations that cannot all be true and spot what future evidence would discriminate among them.

TITLE

GOAL
The body needs to know when available action is complete.

RITUAL
1. Remain Unknown — Name what you have already done, what remains unknown, and which outcomes no longer respond to effort.
2. Boundary — Notice the exact boundary where influence ends.
3. Use Physical — Use one physical closing action and redirect into a present responsibility.

• Use “Boundary” on return.

title: CARRY FORWARD WITHOUT CALLING IT GOOD
goal: Pain can stay true while your response still belongs to you.
steps:
1. State Clearly — State clearly what was wrong or unwanted.
2. Name Boundary — Then name one boundary, skill, loyalty, or value you can carry forward without claiming the event was beneficial.
3. Let Value — Let the value belong to you, not to the harm.
win: ✓ The load shrank to the piece that truly belongs here.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Value”; release extra load.
• Shortcut: “Name Boundary”, once.
• “Name Boundary” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• “State Clearly” to “Let Value”: what loosened?
• I can use “Name Boundary” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: State Clearly → Name Boundary → Let Value
safety:
PAUSE

title: THE LAST-DAY FILTER
goal: Finite life can expose counterfeit urgency.
steps:
1. Imagine Back — Imagine looking back from life’s end—not to frighten yourself, but to rank.
2. Demand — Which current demand disappears?
3. Remain Relationship — Which relationship, integrity choice, health need, or contribution remains?
4. Give Surviving — Give the surviving priority one concrete slot today.
win: ✓ Counterfeit urgency failed the last-day test; one real priority survived.
supports:
• Exhale after “Give Surviving”; slow the clock.
• Loop back? Use “Remain Relationship”.
• “Remain Relationship” puts facts above speed.
• Keep one lesson: “Imagine Back” → “Give Surviving”.
• I can use “Demand” without rushing.
formula_flow: Imagine Back → Demand → Remain Relationship → Give Surviving
safety:
PAUSE
Skip mortality reflection when it intensifies anxiety, grief, or self-harm thoughts.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

content:
TITLE
PAIN IS PRESENT; LIFE HAS OTHER DEPARTMENTS

GOAL
Suffering should not absorb the entire identity budget.

RITUAL
1. Describe Hurting — Say exactly what is hurting.
2. Continue Alongside — Then name three processes continuing alongside it: caring, learning, digesting, noticing, working, resting, relating.
3. Choose Small — Choose one small action from a continuing department without denying the pain.

WIN
✓ Pain stayed real, and another department of life stayed open.

• Gently exhale after “Choose Small”; orient to now.
• On return: “Continue Alongside”.
• “Continue Alongside” moves memory toward then.
• Compare “Describe Hurting” with “Choose Small”.
• I can use “Continue Alongside” while staying in now.

FORMULA FLOW
Describe Hurting → Continue Alongside → Choose Small

PAUSE
Obtain care when pain or distress needs direct treatment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GIVE THE BIG QUESTION A ROOM, NOT THE HOUSE
goal: Existential inquiry needs boundaries to coexist with living.
steps:
1. Set the Room — Choose a short time for the big question.
2. Bring One Question — think about one clear question and stop when the time ends. You do not require a final answer.
3. Return To Life — Then do one normal task that shows how you want to live now.
win: ✓ The big question got a room; the rest of life kept the house.
supports:
• Exhale after “Return To Life”; watch the thought.
• On return, repeat “Bring One Question”.
• “Bring One Question” proves thought is observable.
• “Set the Room” versus “Return To Life”: what eased?
• I can use “Bring One Question” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Set the Room → Bring One Question → Return To Life

title: MOVE THE VALUE TO A NEW VESSEL
goal: Loss may destroy the channel, not the underlying value.
steps:
1. Name Lost — Name what the lost person, role, place, or ability allowed you to express—care, mastery, belonging, beauty, service.
2. Find Different — Find a different, honest channel for a small portion of that value.
3. Start — Begin without treating substitution as replacement.
win: ✓ The value found a new vessel without pretending nothing was lost.
supports:
• Exhale after “Start”; keep the compass.
• Loop back? Use “Find Different”.
• “Find Different” keeps meaning in motion.
• “Start”: what changed from “Name Lost”?
• I can use “Find Different” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Name Lost → Find Different → Start
safety:
PAUSE
Do not rush reconstruction before the loss has been acknowledged.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAKE THE ORDINARY WORTHY OF FULL CONTACT
goal: Sacredness can be an attention quality, not an exceptional event.
steps:
1. Choose Routine — Choose one routine act—making tea, bathing, preparing a child’s bag, opening work.
2. Perform — do it without rushing or secondary media.
3. Craft — Notice craft, dependence, and life supported by the act.
4. Finish Deserved — Finish as if it deserved completion.
win: ✓ Ordinary task, full contact. It got the finish it deserved.
supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Deserved”; slow the clock.
• Use “Craft” on return.
• “Craft” puts facts above speed.
• Difference check: “Choose Routine” → “Finish Deserved”.
• I can use “Perform” without rushing.

title: WHAT PREPARATION DID WORRY ACTUALLY PRODUCE?
goal: Imagined work should show a deliverable.
steps:

2. Separate Useful — Separate useful actions from repeated simulation.
3. Prepare Name — If the list contains a real gap, prepare once.
4. Remain Name — If no gap remains, label further worry UNPAID OVERTIME.
win: ✓ Worry produced no new deliverable. Overtime cancelled.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Remain Name”; orient to now.
• If it flares, choose “Prepare Name”.
• “Prepare Name” moves memory toward then.
• What lost power: “Create Worry” → “Remain Name”?
• I can use “Separate Useful” while staying in now.

title: MARK THE QUALITY DROP
goal: Analysis needs an exit before fatigue corrupts it.
steps:
1. Repeat No — Define your personal decline signs in advance: rereading, harsher certainty, slower comprehension, repeated searches, no new distinctions.
2. Stop Last — When two appear, stop and hold the last reliable conclusion.
3. Start Recovery — Recovery precedes any reopening.
win: ✓ I caught the moment thinking quality dropped and exited before fatigue took over.
supports:

• On return: “Stop Last”.
• “Stop Last” widens the evidence field.
• “Start Recovery”: what changed from “Repeat No”?
• I can use “Stop Last” before concluding.
formula_flow: Repeat No → Stop Last → Start Recovery
safety:
PAUSE
Continue only when delay creates greater risk than reduced quality.

title: NAME THE GUARANTEE YOU ARE SECRETLY BUYING
goal: Research may be serving emotional certainty, not information.
steps:
1. Finish Sentence — Finish this sentence: ‘If I keep checking, I hope to guarantee that…’ Ask whether any amount of data can provide that emotional promise.
2. Remain Demand — Gather only information that changes action; treat the remaining demand as uncertainty to carry.
win: ✓ Useful information ended where the guarantee-seeking began.

• Pulled back? Touch “Remain Demand”.
• “Finish Sentence” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Finish Sentence” to “Remain Demand”: what loosened?
• I can use “Remain Demand” without a guarantee.

title: REPLAY THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
goal: Find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation.
steps:
1. Recall Exchange — Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.
2. Halve Speed — Replay it once in imagination at half speed. Keep only what you can actually observe: words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. Shift — Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’
4. Keep Fact — Keep that one fact. End the replay before building another explanation.
win: ✓ The worry cycle lost its automatic restart.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Keep Fact”; orient to now.
• Use “Shift” on return.
• “Shift” moves memory toward then.
• What lost power: “Recall Exchange” → “Keep Fact”?
• I can use “Halve Speed” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Recall Exchange → Halve Speed → Shift → Keep Fact
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if replay raises distress, becomes compulsive, or concerns abuse or danger that requires support and protection.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: AUCTION THE NEXT ATTENTION BLOCK
goal: Limited attention needs a clear way to choose.
steps:
1. Let Active — Let each active concern bid on urgency, consequence, reversibility, and information value.
2. Total — Total the four ratings.
3. Protect Block — Award one protected block to the highest bidder and deny all others entry until time expires.
4. Update Evidence — Re-auction with updated evidence.
win: ✓ My next attention block went to the highest-value bidder.
supports:
• Exhale after “Update Evidence”; slow the clock.
• Pulled back? Touch “Protect Block”.
• “Protect Block” puts facts above speed.
• Compare “Let Active” with “Update Evidence”.
• I can use “Total” without rushing.

title: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
goal: A five-tile loop is much easier to catch.
steps:
1. No Sentences — Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.
2. Imagine Five Signs — Give each of the last five thought turns one simple inner picture.
3. Spot The Return — Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later.
4. Choose An Exit — At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining.
win: ✓ Five icons exposed the repeat—and one place to exit.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose An Exit”; end the lap.
• If it flares, choose “Spot The Return”.
• “Spot The Return” proves loops can stop.
• Look back: “No Sentences” → “Choose An Exit”.
• I can use “Imagine Five Signs” without another lap.
formula_flow: No Sentences → Imagine Five Signs → Spot The Return → Choose An Exit
safety:
PAUSE
Do not imagine this while driving; stop if the mental sequence becomes compulsive, perfectionistic, or more distressing than the thought.

GOAL
A five-tile loop is much easier to catch.

RITUAL
1. No Sentences — Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.
2. Imagine Five Signs — Give each of the last five thought turns one simple inner picture.
3. Spot The Return — Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later.
4. Choose An Exit — At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining.

WIN
✓ Five icons exposed the repeat—and one place to exit.

• Exhale after “Choose An Exit”; end the lap.
• If it flares, choose “Spot The Return”.
• “Spot The Return” proves loops can stop.
• Look back: “No Sentences” → “Choose An Exit”.
• I can use “Imagine Five Signs” without another lap.

FORMULA FLOW
No Sentences → Imagine Five Signs → Spot The Return → Choose An Exit

PAUSE
Do not imagine this while driving; stop if the mental sequence becomes compulsive, perfectionistic, or more distressing than the thought.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DEMOTE THE HEADLINE EXPERIENCE
goal: Foreground and background can share equal status.
steps:
1. Hold Sensation — Hold the dominant sensation or thought with three background what you notices—one sound, one contact point, one visual feature.
2. Give Attention — For a contained interval, give all four equal attentional weight without imagining a separate watcher.
3. Demote the Headline — Notice how centrality changes.
win: ✓ Headline demoted. The background gets equal screen time now.
supports:

• Skip replay; use “Give Attention”.
• “Give Attention” proves thought is observable.
• Difference check: “Hold Sensation” → “Demote the Headline”.
• I can use “Give Attention” without obeying thought.

title: WHERE EXACTLY IS THE OBSERVER?
goal: Test whether the witness has a fixed address.
steps:
1. Search Carefully — Search carefully for the boundary, size, and location of the one who observes.
2. Check Behind — Check behind the eyes, chest, head, and surrounding field.
3. Observe Found — Every found sensation is itself observed.
4. Rest Inability — Rest with the inability to locate a final point.
win: ✓ The sentence stayed, but it stopped being the whole self.
supports:
• Exhale after “Rest Inability”; release extra load.
• Pulled back? Touch “Observe Found”.
• “Observe Found” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Keep one lesson: “Search Carefully” → “Rest Inability”.
• I can use “Check Behind” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Search Carefully → Check Behind → Observe Found → Rest Inability
safety:
PAUSE
Do not continue if location inquiry provokes feeling unreal or detached from yourself.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CATCH THE MOMENT ‘MINE’ ARRIVES
goal: Ownership may be added after experience begins.
steps:

win: ✓ Experience arrived first. Ownership arrived second.

• I can use “Catch Ownership” without obeying thought.

title: SOFTEN BOTH SIDES OF SEEING
goal: Perceiver and perceived need not stay rigidly opposed.
steps:
1. Choose Simple — Choose a simple object or sound.
2. Attend Time — Attend at the shared time to its qualities and the act of perceiving.
3. Place Reality — Refuse to place all reality on either side.
4. Let Relationship — Let the relationship event—seeing or hearing—become primary for several seconds.
win: ✓ Seeing became a relationship, not a rigid split.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Relationship”; watch the thought.
• If it flares, choose “Place Reality”.
• “Place Reality” proves thought is observable.
• Look back: “Choose Simple” → “Let Relationship”.
• I can use “Attend Time” without obeying thought.

title: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
goal: Let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound.
steps:
1. Choose Skill — Choose one familiar, low-risk task with clear external feedback.
2. Centre Feedback — Put sight, touch, sound, or the work result in the centre of attention.
3. Demote Voice — When self-commentary appears, let it continue faintly at the edge without answering or silencing it.
4. Finish Unit — Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections.
win: ✓ Commentary moved to the cheap seat; the moment kept centre stage.
supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Unit”; mark the pause.
• If it flares, choose “Demote Voice”.
• “Demote Voice” proves choice interrupted habit.
• “Finish Unit”: what changed from “Choose Skill”?
• I can use “Centre Feedback” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Choose Skill → Centre Feedback → Demote Voice → Finish Unit

title: ROTATE THE OBSERVATION DECK
goal: Every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent.
steps:
1. Observe Moment — Observe the same moment from three positions: body-centred, environment-centred, and whole-field.
2. Spot Amplifier — Keep what each amplifies and hides.
3. Choose Position — Choose the position best suited to the upcoming task rather than declaring any one neutral.
win: ✓ Perspective became a tool for the task, not a claim of neutrality.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Position”; watch the thought.
• Catch restart with “Spot Amplifier”.
• “Spot Amplifier” proves thought is observable.
• Keep one lesson: “Observe Moment” → “Choose Position”.
• I can use “Spot Amplifier” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Observe Moment → Spot Amplifier → Choose Position

steps:

title: PLAY EMOTION JENGA
goal: Pull one feeling from the stack and see what is actually holding.
steps:
1. Name Stack — Name two or three feelings and place each on a separate mental block.
2. Pull One — Temporarily bracket one block with the phrase ‘not deleted—just outside this test.’
3. Check Remainder — Observe what changes in the remainder: body location, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all. Keep one difference.
4. Rebuild Stack — Restore the removed block. Repeat only if useful, then rebuild the complete stack before finishing.
win: ✓ The emotional stack revealed which block was actually carrying the weight.
supports:
• Exhale after “Rebuild Stack”; mark the pause.
• Shortcut: “Check Remainder”, once.
• “Check Remainder” proves choice interrupted habit.
• What lost power: “Name Stack” → “Rebuild Stack”?
• I can use “Pull One” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Name Stack → Pull One → Check Remainder → Rebuild Stack
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the game causes numbness, feeling unreal or disconnected, suppression, or pressure to erase a valid feeling.

steps:

2. Feel Arrange — Arrange them as they feel now.

4. Name Real — Name the real-life action equivalent to that move.
win: ✓ The abstract problem moved on the table—and revealed a real-world move.
supports:

• Loop back? Use “Move Object”.
• “Move Object” moves memory toward then.
• Look back: “Use Small” → “Name Real”.
• I can use “Feel Arrange” while staying in now.

title: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
goal: Resistance may be protecting something your plan ignored.
steps:
1. Give Obstacle — Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting?
2. Ask Fear — What do you fear will happen?
3. Make Step — What would make one step acceptable?
4. Picture Negotiate — Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control.
win: ✓ Resistance revealed the need it was trying to protect.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Picture Negotiate”; orient to now.
• Loop back? Use “Make Step”.
• “Make Step” moves memory toward then.
• “Give Obstacle” versus “Picture Negotiate”: what eased?
• I can use “Ask Fear” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Give Obstacle → Ask Fear → Make Step → Picture Negotiate
safety:
PAUSE
Do not personify intrusive voices or experiences if that worsens symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: OPEN THREE ENDING ROOMS
goal: The future should not be rehearsed as a single locked corridor.
steps:
1. Identify Critical — Spot the critical decision point in the dominant future scene.
2. Create Endings — Create three endings by changing the choice there: cautious, courageous, and collaborative.
3. Cost — Notice the cost and value of each.
4. Keep Best — Keep the ending that best fits evidence and values.
win: ✓ The compass still works even when the landscape hurts.
supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Best”; keep the compass.
• Loop back? Use “Cost”.
• “Cost” keeps meaning in motion.
• “Keep Best”: what changed from “Identify Critical”?
• I can use “Create Endings” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Identify Critical → Create Endings → Cost → Keep Best

OPEN THREE ENDING ROOMS

GOAL
The future should not be rehearsed as a single locked corridor.

RITUAL
1. Identify Critical — Spot the critical decision point in the dominant future scene.
2. Create Endings — Create three endings by changing the choice there: cautious, courageous, and collaborative.
3. Cost — Notice the cost and value of each.
4. Keep Best — Keep the ending that best fits evidence and values.

WIN
✓ The compass still works even when the landscape hurts.

• Exhale after “Keep Best”; keep the compass.
• Loop back? Use “Cost”.
• “Cost” keeps meaning in motion.
• “Keep Best”: what changed from “Identify Critical”?
• I can use “Create Endings” while pain stays real.

FORMULA FLOW
Identify Critical → Create Endings → Cost → Keep Best

PAUSE
Do not imagine unsafe endings merely to increase variety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHANGE THE SYMBOL’S JOB
goal: Unspoken experience may respond to transformation before explanation.
steps:
1. Choose Image — Choose the image or object that represents the state.
2. Open Cage — Alter one property—open the cage, cool the metal, add roots, repair the crack, move the weight, give the storm a shoreline.
3. Observe Inner — Observe the inner response and translate it into one practical move.
win: ✓ The mind produced content; it did not produce a commander.
supports:
• Exhale after “Observe Inner”; watch the thought.
• Restart detected: “Open Cage”.
• “Open Cage” proves thought is observable.
• Compare “Choose Image” with “Observe Inner”.
• I can use “Open Cage” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Choose Image → Open Cage → Observe Inner
safety:
PAUSE
End the exercise when imagery grows disturbing, bizarre, or detached from reality.

title: MOVE THE INNER CAMERA
goal: Helplessness may be held in one visual angle.
steps:
1. Adjust — Adjust the internal scene’s distance, height, direction, and frame one at a time.
2. Test Far — Test close, far, eye-level, above, behind, wide, and cropped.
3. Choose Angle — Choose the angle that preserves facts while increasing present choice.
win: ✓ The facts stayed put while the camera found more choice.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Angle”; watch the thought.
• Skip replay; use “Test Far”.
• “Test Far” proves thought is observable.
• Compare “Adjust” with “Choose Angle”.
• I can use “Test Far” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Adjust → Test Far → Choose Angle
safety:
PAUSE
Traumatic visual work should be brief and supported when necessary.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

TITLE
MOVE THE INNER CAMERA

GOAL
Helplessness may be held in one visual angle.

RITUAL
1. Adjust — Adjust the internal scene’s distance, height, direction, and frame one at a time.
2. Test Far — Test close, far, eye-level, above, behind, wide, and cropped.
3. Choose Angle — Choose the angle that preserves facts while increasing present choice.

title: FOUR-CELL DECISION MATRIX
goal: Separate value from danger before emotion blends them.
steps:
1. Score Option — Score each option on value alignment, downside, reversibility, and learning.
2. Add Sentence — Add a sentence explaining every score.
3. Compare Patterns — Compare patterns rather than relying on the total alone.
4. Prefer Option — Favour the option with containable risk while important value is expressed.

title: WHICH REGRET ARE YOU AVOIDING?
goal: Regret has four species with different advice.
steps:
1. Estimate Regret — For each option, estimate regret of action, inaction, delay, and self-betrayal.
2. Describe Future — Say the future scene behind the highest score.
3. Ask Regret — Ask which regret is reversible and which conflicts most with your values.
win: ✓ Regret split into types, and only one deserved to guide the choice.
supports:

• On return, repeat “Describe Future”.
• “Describe Future” keeps meaning in motion.
• “Ask Regret”: what changed from “Estimate Regret”?
• I can use “Describe Future” while pain stays real.

title: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
goal: Crowded choices get clearer when only two enter each round.
steps:
1. Seed Options — Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Pick Criterion — Choose one criterion that matters for this round and picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Play Pairs — Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown Next — Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.
win: ✓ I let two options enter each round until one earned the next move.
supports:
• Exhale after “Crown Next”; release the score.
• On return, repeat “Play Pairs”.
• “Play Pairs” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• What lost power: “Seed Options” → “Crown Next”?
• I can use “Pick Criterion” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Seed Options → Pick Criterion → Play Pairs → Crown Next
safety:

WIN
✓ I let two options enter each round until one earned the next move.

• Exhale after “Crown Next”; release the score.
• On return, repeat “Play Pairs”.
• “Play Pairs” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• What lost power: “Seed Options” → “Crown Next”?
• I can use “Pick Criterion” without perfecting.

FORMULA FLOW
Seed Options → Pick Criterion → Play Pairs → Crown Next

PAUSE
For high-stakes choices, use the winner only as the next research step and include qualified advice and all safety criteria.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REMOVE WHAT THE CHOICE WOULD ‘PROVE’
goal: Identity signalling can distort an otherwise practical decision.
steps:
1. Say About — Name what each option would supposedly say about you—successful, loyal, brave, weak, ordinary.
2. Cross Out — Strike through those identity messages mentally.
3. Check Again — Re-check only consequences, values, constraints, and evidence.
4. Notice Shift — Notice whether the preferred option changes.
win: ✓ Identity stepped out of the voting booth; the practical choice became clearer.
supports:
• Exhale after “Notice Shift”; keep the compass.
• Catch restart with “Check Again”.
• “Check Again” keeps meaning in motion.
• “Notice Shift”: what changed from “Say About”?
• I can use “Cross Out” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Say About → Cross Out → Check Again → Notice Shift
safety:
PAUSE
Identity and community may be legitimate values; distinguish them from performance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE PAST INVESTMENT GETS NO NEW VOTE
goal: Sunk cost is history, not future value.
steps:
1. Hide Already — Hide what has already been spent.
2. Compare Options — Compare options from today forward using remaining cost, likely benefit, opportunity cost, and risk.
3. Remove Sunk Vote — Reveal the past investment afterward only for learning, never for sharing.
win: ✓ The past investment stayed in history and lost its vote on the future.
supports:
• Exhale after “Remove Sunk Vote”; slow the clock.
• On return: “Compare Options”.
• “Compare Options” puts facts above speed.
• At “Remove Sunk Vote”, compare “Hide Already”.
• I can use “Compare Options” without rushing.

content:
TITLE
THE PAST INVESTMENT GETS NO NEW VOTE

GOAL
Sunk cost is history, not future value.

RITUAL
1. Hide Already — Hide what has already been spent.
2. Compare Options — Compare options from today forward using remaining cost, likely benefit, opportunity cost, and risk.
3. Remove Sunk Vote — Reveal the past investment afterward only for learning, never for sharing.

WIN
✓ The past investment stayed in history and lost its vote on the future.

• Exhale after “Remove Sunk Vote”; slow the clock.
• On return: “Compare Options”.
• “Compare Options” puts facts above speed.
• At “Remove Sunk Vote”, compare “Hide Already”.
• I can use “Compare Options” without rushing.

FORMULA FLOW
Hide Already → Compare Options → Remove Sunk Vote

PAUSE
Account for contractual or reputational consequences that genuinely persist.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CONSTRAINTS ENTER BEFORE OPTIONS
goal: Must-have limits should shape the field before desire fills it.
steps:
1. Picture Safety — Picture safety, ethics, consent, resources, and timing constraints first.
2. Eliminate — Eliminate choices that violate them.
3. Generate — Generate options only inside the surviving space.
4. Lead With Constraints — Treat creativity as solving within reality, not arguing with the boundary.
win: ✓ I let the constraints shape the field before the options started campaigning.
supports:

• On return, repeat “Generate”.
• “Generate” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• At “Lead With Constraints”, compare “Picture Safety”.
• I can use “Eliminate” without carrying it all.

title: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
goal: A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.
steps:
1. State Rule — Picture the rule without naming who taught it.
2. Change Context — Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.
3. Compare Effects — Compare who is protected, restricted, or harmed in each setting.
4. Keep Core — Keep only the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; notice the rest as conditional.
win: ✓ The rule kept its ethical core and lost its fake universality.
supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Core”; keep both sides.
• Catch restart with “Compare Effects”.
• “Compare Effects” widens the evidence field.
• Difference check: “State Rule” → “Keep Core”.
• I can use “Change Context” before concluding.
formula_flow: State Rule → Change Context → Compare Effects → Keep Core

title: COMMON IS NOT THE SAME AS RIGHT
goal: Frequency cannot settle an ethical question.
steps:
1. State Social — State the social norm and your chosen criteria—harm, fairness, consent, dignity, responsibility.
2. Evaluate — Check the norm against each criterion without citing popularity.
3. Keep Modify — Keep, modify, or reject it based on the ethical comparison.
win: ✓ Popularity lost the argument the moment ethics entered the room.
supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Modify”; drop the scoreboard.
• Loop back? Use “Evaluate”.
• “Evaluate” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Before/after: “State Social” → “Keep Modify”.
• I can use “Evaluate” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: State Social → Evaluate → Keep Modify

title: DO ONE GOOD THING WITH NO APPLAUSE BUTTON
goal: Values can survive the absence of approval.
steps:
1. Choose Safe — do a low-risk act you endorse and do it without announcing, checking reactions, or fishing for extra certainty.
2. Let Discomfort — Let the discomfort of no feedback rise and change.
3. Review Quietly — Review the action by your values once it is done.
win: ✓ I did one good thing with no audience and it still counted.
supports:

• Skip replay; use “Let Discomfort”.
• “Let Discomfort” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• Before/after: “Choose Safe” → “Review Quietly”.
• I can use “Let Discomfort” without a guarantee.

title: HIDE THE CROWD’S ANSWER

steps:

3. View Crowd — Reveal social proof afterward and change your view only if the crowd supplies new evidence, not mere numbers.

steps:

title: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
goal: A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.
steps:
1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where it does not fit.
5. Shrink the Rule — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.
win: ✓ The belief got a postcode instead of a passport to everywhere.

• I can use “Imagine Four Limits” without owning everything.

content:
TITLE
GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE

GOAL
A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.

RITUAL
1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where it does not fit.
5. Shrink the Rule — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.

WIN
✓ The belief got a postcode instead of a passport to everywhere.

• Exhale after “Shrink the Rule”; release extra blame.
• Catch restart with “Test Inside”.
• “Test Outside” keeps blame in proportion.
• What changed: “Name The Belief” → “Shrink the Rule”?
• I can use “Imagine Four Limits” without owning everything.

FORMULA FLOW
Name The Belief → Imagine Four Limits → Test Inside → Test Outside → Shrink the Rule

PAUSE
Do not use belief boundaries to minimise abuse, discrimination, medical facts, legal duties, or immediate danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
